1 Introduction 
1.1 Project description 
[C11-GENE-010001]  
The 525 kV – 2000 MW projects - Fécamp Grand Large 1 (HA1), Fécamp Grand Large 2 (HA2) and 
Golfe du Lion Centre (GLC) and Bretagne Nord Ouest (BNO) - in the framework of PPE3 (Plan 
Pluriannual de l’Energie 3) consists of bipolar HVDC topology for each project with a Guaranteed Active 
Power Link Capacity of 2000 MW and a rated DC voltage of ± 525 kV using Voltage Source Converter 
for each HVDC Link.  
 
[C11-GENE-010002]  
Each HVDC link – grid connection system – consists of an Offshore Substation, an Onshore Converter 
Station and a HVDC Cable Link (HVDC cables and Dedicated Metallic Return (DMR)) between the two 
stations.

Following requirements regarding seismicity shall be considered: 
The Onshore Converter Station design shall take into account the seismic level of the location (Table 
3). The Onshore Converter Station shall be considered as an installation of category of  IV of  
(Arrete_22102010_Seismic)  (this category includes installations whose protection is essential for the 
needs of civil security and national defence as well or the maintenance of public order, as such it 
includes public energy distribution centres) and the acceleration considered for the design shall comply 
with (Arrete_22102010_Seismic). 
 
As such and in accordance with article R565-5 of “Code de l’Environnement”, the equipment and 
systems located within the Onshore Converter Stations’ buildings must be capable of remaining in 
service and delivering its performances in case of earthquake.

Power Link Capacity. This power is the Rated Pole Capacity of the HVDC Pole Link.

8.4.2 
Operating mode OM2: symmetrical bipolar 
[CBOD-SYST-100009]  
OM2 is an operating mode where the DMR is not available. In this mode, it is crucial to ensure a perfect 
balance of current on both Converter Poles to prevent any current circulation though the ground. The 
contractor shall propose an effective strategy for a transition from OM1 to OM2 without any power 
interruption, even in case of DMR fault detection. The proposal needs to be verified and validated by 
Employer. As an example, one possible approach to achieve current balance is by coupling offshore 
AC electrical nodes.

[CBOD-SYST-100010]  
The operating mode OM3, one of the HVDC Pole Link is not available (onshore Converter Pole, Offshore

Operating mode OM5: Round power test for commissioning 
[CBOD-SYST-100011]  
To partially commission the HVDC link when the OWFs are unavailable, the operating mode OM5 is 
required. In this mode, power is continuously circulated between the Onshore and Offshore Converter

Onshore Converter Pole to its corresponding Offshore Converter Pole and then returned to the Onshore 
Converter Station via other Converter Pole. The maximum power that can be sent shall be proposed by 
Contractor to Employer to not exceed the rating of DMR cable.

8.4.6.3 Restart requirement 
[C11-SYST-010073]  
Duration requirements for restart are described hereafter for different situations: 
- 
Trip in an energised state of the entire Converter Station, of a single pole of Converter Station, 
HVDC Pole Link and HVDC Link: less than 30 minutes. Contractor shall optimize the duration 
depending on the equipment ratings and states (e.g.: charging state of valves, temperature of 
pre-insertion resistor, etc.). Contractor may highlight a critical charging state enabling a quick 
restart (less than 3 minutes). 
- 
Trip at early stage of starting sequence where the Converter and HVDC Link have not yet been 
charged up to a critical point: as fast as possible and less than 3 minutes.

Automatic reactive power adaptation after trip of one HVDC Pole Link 
[B21ai-VORE-110165] 
In case of trip of a HVDC Pole Link, the total reactive power of both Converter Poles shall be maintained 
and the resultant Q shall be the sum of Q_setpoint of both Converter Poles before the trip (as long as 
the maximum reactive capacity or the remaining Converter Pole or its OQR is respected).  
 
The automatic adaptation can be enabled/disabled.  
 
The adaption shall be by default disabled in case of SPM with 2 electrical nodes on Onshore Converter 
Station.  
 
In U-mode, reactive power injection in case of the trip of a Converter Pole shall be adapted by voltage 
control.

The insulation coordination of the HVDC Link shall be carried out by Converter System Contractor for

[CBOD-CPSY-100154]

monitoring, control, protection, status display, sequence of event recording and data reporting. The C&P

operation, i.e. the Onshore and Offshore Stations are usually not manned and are only controlled, 
monitored and trouble-shot via the remote control and remote access.

PCM network and the Utility network respectively, each network must be physically separate from the 
others. Therefore:

The networks shall not have any physical element in common. 
- 
The EC optical fibers connecting the onshore and offshore components of each network must 
be allocated for the sole use of that network.

The Contractor shall provide a Long-Term Asset Replacement Plan (LTARP). The LTARP shall provide 
an insight into the condition and expected degradation of all equipment forming part of the Works and, 
as such, the overall life and expected replacement (or refurbishment) period of assets. Disposal of 
equipment shall also be described. It shall provide guidelines regarding the optimum timing of 
refurbishment and replacement in terms of life-cycle management for all components or equipment.

scope of these Works.  In addition to converter components (i.e. cooling systems, valve components, 
HV equipment, control and protection equipment), is shall also include the components defined in the 
civil works (B22b_i).

[B22c-VALV-910096]-N3  
A valve mock-up shall be provided by the Contractor in order for the Employer personnel to develop and 
manage in-house skills and know-how regarding preventive and curative maintenance of the power 
electronics valves. 
The valve mock-up shall be a true-to-life full-size (scale 1:1) replica of one valve tower or equivalent 
valve structure, such that working conditions (height, weight, equipment accessibility, etc.) are exactly 
the same as on the actual power electronics valves. All equipment related to the valves such as earthing 
points, water pipes, grading electrodes, cable trays, insulators, fibre optics, etc.… shall be included in 
the mock-up.

1.2 Pos 20 SSTI part 1 Screening  
1.2.1 
Scope 
The goal of this study is to evaluate the possibility of Sub-Synchronous Torsional Interaction (SSTI) 
between synchronous generators and the SunCable HVDC PLUS. The study ensures that there is no 
detrimental interaction between the HVDC PLUS converter controls and the generator-shaft-systems 
in the sub-synchronous frequency range.  
The objective of the screening study (SSTI Part 1) is the following: 
• 
To identify specific thermal generators, for which SSTI between the generator and the HVDC 
PLUS converter is probable, in a screening study based on the calculation of Unit Interaction 
Factors (UIF), as defined by EPRI.

PLUS converter is probable, in a screening study based on the calculation of Unit Interaction 
Factors (UIF), as defined by EPRI.  
 
1.2.2 
Methodology 
For the evaluation of the risk of SSTI between a generator and a converter station, the following study 
methods are applied: 
• 
In the first step, the Unit Interaction Factors (UIF) for all generators under consideration is 
determined (“screening study”). This is a simple method to check the probability of SSTI. The 
output of the screening study is a list of generators which shall be analysed in a detailed study 
in time domain due to high UIF values.  
• 
The screening study relies on stationary short-circuit calculations. The HVDC modelling does 
not have influence on the screening study results. HVDC or FACTS devices are considered to 
have no short circuit contribution according to IEC 60909.

Development of a preliminary PSS/e model, which is used for stability type studies, including 
modelling of the control required for phasor type digital models to investigate symmetric faults. All

loops of electromagnetic transient nature and acting in a transient range (time constants less than

power system simulations, in which the AC power system is typically represented by a positive-
sequence equivalent. DC Converters are represented by simplified equations and are not modelled to 
switching device level.

1 Introduction 
 
The LS Power HVDC Project is a project designed to enhance the reliability of the electrical grid 
in the heart of San José by introducing a powerful, new energy source to the region. Its purpose 
is to bolster economic growth and improve accessibility to cost-effective, renewable energy to 
cater to the demands of local residents and businesses. The project, situated in Santa Clara 
County, California.

2 Scope of work & methodology 
 
2.1 Pos 10: Preliminary Digital RMS Model 1GW link 
2.1.1 Scope 
The Consultant will adjust and parametrized the existing PSLF HVDCPL2 rms model and deliver a 
preliminary rms model of the LS Power HVDC PLUS, in PSLF. The field of application is mainly in 
studies related to power system stability and investigations on the power system electro-mechanical 
dynamics. In such studies the AC power system is typically represented by the positive sequence. 
The HVDC PLUS model represents the converter performance for the positive sequence. All 
functions related to unbalanced system functions are not part of the model implementation. Very 
fast control loops acting in a transient range cannot be implemented in detail.

ositive sequence. All 
functions related to unbalanced system functions are not part of the model implementation. Very 
fast control loops acting in a transient range cannot be implemented in detail.  
The model will be developed in two project stages:  
• 
The 500 MW stage, where the 1GW rated link will have current limitations that limit the 
operation to close to 500MVA (exact values to be provided). 
• 
The final stage, where the 1GW rated link will have the typical current limitations that allow 
for operation at 1 GW. 
Siemens Energy will provide guidance on the value of the current limitations.  
2.1.2 Data input from the Employer 
• 
Main Circuit parameters of the LS Power HVDC  
• 
Point of common coupling information (e.g., Fault levels and X/R ratios) 
2.1.3 Methodology 
The model includes control functions, which are relevant for stability investigations, such as: 
• 
Active power control and limitations, frequency control 
• 
Reactive power control and limitations, AC volt

el includes control functions, which are relevant for stability investigations, such as: 
• 
Active power control and limitations, frequency control 
• 
Reactive power control and limitations, AC voltage control, fast reactive current injection for 
fault ride through 
• 
Grid following controls 
2.1.4 Exclusions: 
• 
The model will not be suitable for simulation of DC faults or other converter internal faults. 
However, a converter or pole trip can be simulated to emulate a DC faults. 
• 
The model will not be suitable for simulation of un-symmetric AC faults. 
• 
Modelling of the Converter Control is partly simplified to enable a suitable time step for 
power system analysis. 
The preliminary digital stability Model in PSLF will be suitable for typical applications in power 
system studies. 
2.1.5 Dynamic Tests 
For the purpose of the verification of the Digital Stability Model, the dynamic response of the RMS 
model for a set of benchmark cases will be tested.

PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 
2.1 General 
1) All requirements stated in this PTS are the minimum requirements that the HVDC System 
shall meet. The CONTRACTOR shall make available the complete inherent capability of 
the HVDC System. The control and protection system shall be designed based on the 
actual technical capability of the HVDC System. 
2) All references shall be at the PCC-AC or PCC-DC of the HVDC Converter Stations unless 
otherwise stated. 
3) Regardless of the topology of the HVDC System, the HVDC System shall remain robust 
to events and shall provide sufficiently strong voltage source and synchronizing 
frequency to allow all IBR and loads connected to the AC networks in the electrical vicinity 
of the HVDC System's PCC-ACs to remain stable. 
4) Extreme ambient temperatures in excess of those identified in this PTS may occur.

2.2 Operating Modes 
1) The HVDC System shall be capable of operation in the following Operating Modes: 
a) Mode 1 Bipole: This is the normal operating mode. In this mode of operation both 
Poles can exchange active and reactive power with the AC networks. When in Bipole 
mode, both poles are connected to the DMR. It shall be possible to operate each Pole 
entirely independently of the other when in Bipole mode including one pole 
transferring power in one direction and the other in the opposite direction (known as 
Round Power), limited only by the capability of the neutral equipment.

b) Mode 2 Rigid Bipole: In this mode of operation both Poles can exchange active and/or 
reactive power with the AC networks but there is no connection to the DMR.  
c) Mode 3 Asymmetric Monopole, Pole 1: In this mode of operation Pole 1 can exchange 
active and/or reactive power with the AC networks with the DC current return path 
through the DMR. The converters of Pole 2 may either be switched off or operate in 
STATCOM mode.  
d) Mode 4 Asymmetric Monopole, Pole 2: In this mode of operation Pole 2 can exchange 
active and/or reactive power with the AC networks with the DC current return path 
through the DMR. The converters of Pole 1 may either be switched off or operate in

2.3.4 Active Power Capability 
1) Each Converter Pole shall be capable of continuously transmitting 1500MW as measured 
at the PCC-AC of the receiving end station when operating in Asymmetric Monopole 
mode. 
2) The HVDC Converter Stations shall be capable of continuously transmitting 3000MW as 
measured at the PCC-AC of the receiving end station when operating in Bipole mode or 
Rigid Bipole mode. 
3) There shall be no minimum limit on real power transfer for a Converter Pole or the HVDC 
Converter Stations.

components from damage if physical parameters (e.g., cooling water temperature) exceed 
their normal operation window, or when the overload capability has been used completely.

2.4.1 General 
1) The HVDC Converter Stations shall be capable of being put into service, being taken out 
of service, remaining connected to the AC network, maintaining normal operation, and 
meeting all requirements of this PTS under any combination of the AC network conditions 
described below.

1) The HVDC Converter Stations shall be capable of being put into service, being taken out 
of service, remaining connected to the AC network, maintaining normal operation, and 
meeting all requirements of this PTS when the voltage at the PCC-AC is within the voltage 
ranges and time periods as specified in Table 19 and Table 20.

2.4.9 Grid Forming Capability 
1) The HVDC system in coordination with non-synchronous generation shall be capable 
of providing grid forming capability at the PCC-AC. 
2) The HVDC system shall be capable of behaving as a voltage source behind an 
impedance during normal operation and under disturbance. The converter shall have 
an instantaneous response to changes in the grid (e.g., voltage, frequency and voltage 
phase jumps). 
3) During a grid disturbance, the HVDC system shall provide inertia and reactive current 
injection to support the grid frequency and voltage based on grid and converter 
impedances. 
4) Transition to and from grid forming shall be bump-less and shall not require any 
intervention or action by the Operator.

2.5.1.7 Requirements with respect to Faults in the AC Networks 
1) CONTRACTOR shall ensure that the HVDC System’s behavior, when subject to AC system 
faults, meets as a minimum the following requirements: 
a) The Converter Poles shall stay connected according to the fault ride through 
requirements, 
b) The Converter Poles shall be capable of providing support during AC system faults, 
c) AC faults shall not facilitate the transfer of harmonics and/or inter-harmonics to the 
DC side, nor shall the VSC unit inject unacceptable levels of harmonic currents and 
or voltages into the DC side during any AC disturbance.

gapless metal oxide surge arresters, located at different points of the converter station. 
Protective air gaps will not be accepted in the DC or in the AC part of the station.  
2) The appropriate location of the arrester with respect to the equipment to be protected is very 
important.

2.9 Control System Functions and Performances 
2.9.1 General 
1) The CONTRACTOR shall design the HVDC Control and Protection System in line with the 
requirements of this PTS, considering the operational concept, various AC system conditions 
(e.g., varying system strength and other connected elements), the whole range of credible 
combination of system and environmental parameters and ensuring satisfactory 
performance against disturbances.

text:
g., varying system strength and other connected elements), the whole range of credible 
combination of system and environmental parameters and ensuring satisfactory 
performance against disturbances. 
2) The CONTRACTOR shall design the HVDC Control and Protection system to be robust 
considering the potential future expansion of the grid including increased penetration of IBRs 
and reduced short circuit level.   
3) All control modes shall ensure that the Converter Poles respects their physical limits (current, 
over/under-voltage) and that of all adjoining grid elements. 
4) The controls shall minimize generation of inter-harmonics. Furthermore, the controls shall not 
facilitate the transfer or coupling of harmonics between the AC and DC-sides. 
2.10 Converter Control Modes 
1) This section functionally describes the basic and distinct control modes at the converter level. 
The CONTRACTOR shall as a minimum deliver all these control modes.

2.25.2 MTDC Control and Protection Requirements 
1) One converter shall operate in constant DC voltage control mode. The AC network connected 
to the converter operating in constant DC voltage control mode must have the capability to 
tolerate power changes. The other converters will operate in power control mode. A converter 
may operate in AC frequency and voltage control mode when the converter is connected to 
an islanded network on the AC side. In this situation the converter will absorb or generate the 
power required by the islanded network. Thus, there is no direct control of the power since 
the converter is operating as a swing bus on the AC side.

1) CONTRACTOR shall deliver suitably linearized small-signal models of the 
converter system. These models shall include all poles and zeros of the transfer 
functions that represent the MIMO model of the converter stations in the 
frequency range of at least 0.2 Hz – 3000 Hz. 
2) CONTRACTOR shall at least consider the two possible representation formats 
described below for the delivery of the small-signal models: 
a) State-space representation defined by the A, B, C, and D matrices.

5.3 Short Circuit Study 
 
1) CONTRACTOR shall perform Short Circuit Study to evaluate the maximum and 
minimum short circuit currents in the network, in and around the point of 
common coupling (PCC) of the HVDC converter station. The main reference to 
be adhered to by CONTRACTOR for the short circuit current evaluation is IEC-
60909. 
2) CONTRACTOR shall follow the assumptions related to voltage factor C as per 
IEC-60909 as follows: 
a) Cmax = 1.10 shall be used to calculate the maximum short circuit currents. 
This will help estimate the expected maximum current stress and determine 
the corresponding withstand capability of equipment, as well as the breaking 
capacity of circuit breakers. 
b) Cmin = 1.00 shall be applied to calculate the minimum short circuit currents.

1)  The scope of this study is to evaluate the performance of the HVDC system 
during significant system voltage unbalances, such as single line-to-ground 
faults or other line faults on the AC side. Special care shall be taken to the 
performance when one or several of the controllable elements in the HVDC reach 
their capability limits (e.g., voltage or current limits). The scope covers the 
development of a robust operational strategy that allows the HVDC system to

5.12.2 Definitions 
 
1) Temporary overvoltage (TOV) 
The power frequency overvoltage of relatively long duration as per IEC 60071-1. 
This can originate from faults, switching operations such as load rejection, 
resonance conditions, non-linearity (Ferro-resonance), or by a combination of 
these. TOV should not exceed the fundamental frequency withstand voltage for 
any equipment. 
2) Slow Front Overvoltage (SFO) 
These are short duration transient overvoltage of few milliseconds or less and 
more specifically as per IEC 60071-1, with time to peak 20 µs < Tp ≤ 5 000 µs, and 
tail duration T 2 ≤ 20 ms. These are usually highly damped.

transient overvoltage of few milliseconds or less and 
more specifically as per IEC 60071-1, with time to peak 20 µs < Tp ≤ 5 000 µs, and 
tail duration T 2 ≤ 20 ms. These are usually highly damped. These can originate 
from the switching operations of the overhead lines or cables, fault clearing and 
circuit breaker operations etc. 
3)  Fast-Front Overvoltage (FFO) 
Transient overvoltage, usually unidirectional, with time to peak 0,1 µs < T1 ≤ 20 
µs, and tail duration T2 < 300 µs. These can originate from the lightning strike on 
the overhead transmission lines. This includes direct stroke and back flashover.  
4) Very Fast Front Overvoltage (VFFO) 
As per IEC 60071-1, transient overvoltage, usually unidirectional, with time to 
peak Tf ≤ 0,1 µs, and with or without superimposed oscillations at frequency 30 
kHz < f < 100 MHz. These can originate from fault/switching operation of the dis-
connector or circuit breaker in the Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS).

5.14 Ferro-resonance Studies 
 
1) A ferro-resonance study in HVDC systems involves analyzing the phenomenon of 
ferro-resonance, which occurs due to nonlinear interactions between the 
magnetic core of transformers or reactors and capacitances within the system. 
This can lead to abnormal overvoltages, currents, and oscillations that can 
severely damage equipment or disrupt system stability. 
2) Ferro-resonance shall not occur under any conceivable conditions. Additionally, 
if there are any surge capacitors in the GIS, CONTRACTOR shall ensure that no 
such phenomenon occurs.

torsional modes of nearby turbine-generators. These interactions can cause 
sub-synchronous oscillations that may negatively impact turbine-generator 
stability. 
The objective of this study is to verify that the HVDC system does not induce 
sub-synchronous oscillations in nearby turbine-generators. The scope of the 
study is to consider all the nearby turbine-generators, while performing the

SSCI occurs when the control systems of HVDC or other power electronics-
based devices (e.g., SVCs, STATCOMs) interact with series-compensated 
transmission lines, potentially leading to sub-synchronous resonances that 
can cause oscillations and instability.

7.1 HVDC Control Replica Requirements  
7.1.1 General  
1) CONTRACTOR shall supply a set of replica control and protection equipment 
complete with all necessary interfaces “same as per site” to facilitate performing 
simulations and studies on the controls using a Real Time Digital Simulator 
(RTDS). Replica controls do not have to represent redundancy, switchyard 
interlocking, cooling system and auxiliary controls etc., however the complete 
system shall be able to replicate dynamic performance of the HVDC system. 
However, CONTRACTOR shall make sure to provide similar number of panels 
compared to site control and protection hardware.

7.1.2 Replica requirements 
 The replica control and protection system shall consist of the following at the minimum: 
1) The actual software and hardware system of real control and protection system 
shall be used in replica system. The original software can be loaded onto the 
replica system with only minor modifications. For example, redundancy could be 
disabled. 
2) Control and protection systems shall be required at both the station and pole 
levels, along with any additional low-level control cubicles necessary for 
accurately simulating the behavior of the converter valves. All required hardware 
and software for representing the valve modules and necessary interfaces shall 
also be included.

1 Scope of work & methodology 
1.1 Pos 40-a Detailed rms model Power Factory 
Development of a PowerFactory DIgSILENT model, which is used for stability type studies, including 
modelling of the control required for phasor type digital models to investigate symmetric faults. All 
functions related to asymmetric functions are not part of model implementation. Very fast control 
loops acting in a transient range (time constants less than 1 ms) are not implemented in detail. The 
developed model to be delivered is for the use of dynamic power system simulations, in which the AC 
power system is typically represented by a positive sequence equivalent. DC Converters are 
represented by simplified equations and are not modelled to switching device level.

tions, in which the AC 
power system is typically represented by a positive sequence equivalent. DC Converters are 
represented by simplified equations and are not modelled to switching device level. 
Specifically for this project the following control modes will be considered: 
• 
Grid Following Controls (DVC) (El Fadrell Converter station) 
• 
Grid Forming  (San MArtin Converters station) 
A dynamic benchmark of the RMS model will be done against the detailed PSCAD model to validate 
the performance. 
1.1.1 Methodology 
In power system stability studies, the electro-mechanic stability of a power system is evaluated for 
the fundamental frequency. Therefore, the stability model is valid for the use of investigations related 
to the following phenomena: 
• 
Classical stability studies in large, interconnected power systems 
o Rotor angle stability of generators 
o Voltage stability in the power system 
o Frequency stability of the power system 
These phenomena can be studied in the ele

arge, interconnected power systems 
o Rotor angle stability of generators 
o Voltage stability in the power system 
o Frequency stability of the power system 
These phenomena can be studied in the electro-mechanic time frame assuming symmetrical 
conditions. 
• 
Fundamental frequency interactions between the HVDC PLUS and the AC systems to which 
the converter stations are connected. 
Due to the fact, that relatively fast control functions need to be modelled for the HVDC PLUS, a fine 
time step increment of around 1 ms is required. 
The model includes control functions, which are relevant for stability investigations, such as: 
• 
Active power control and limitations, frequency control 
• 
Reactive power control and limitations, AC voltage control 
• 
Reactive power control modes (Q-mode and V-mode) for selected cases 
• 
Emulation of converter block, run-back and run-up (RAS) functions.

1 Introduction
The purpose of this document is to provide a Technical offer for Protection Coordination study of the
Offshore HVDC Wind Parks Lanwin 2, Lanwin 4 and Balwin 3.
2 Scope of work & methodology
2.1
Protection Coordination Offshore Scope
The Protection Coordination study and relay settings will be developed and provided. The following
points will be considered:

The study will be carried out when the SC (Short circuit) model of both PowerFactory and PSCAD
is ready and can be taken as valid for protection coordination studies. PSCAD model should be
received as input from SE GT GS CP SPM and will be used for Prot Coordination Study.

Determine the settings of the protection functions specified for Offshore of the projects Lanwin
2,Lanwin 4 and Balwin 3.

ne the settings of the protection functions specified for Offshore of the projects Lanwin

2.1.1
Methodology

The relay settings will be tested using a combination of PF and PSCAD (Only if benchmark
between models proves that PSCAD is needed). The results from PSCAD and PF models will be
compared for 3ph faults (Symetrical) and the PF short circuit results will be used. For unbalanced
faults (2ph, 1ph-g) the behavior will be compared between PSCAD/PF to determine if PF
asymmetrical RMS simulation is accurate enough (In case it is not then comtrade files will be used
for functions that require them). The comtrade files exported from PSCAD will also be analyzed
using SIGRA.

The RMS 3ph fault simulations will show the dynamic operation and coordination of protection
relays under fault conditions.

1 Introduction 
The TransWest Express (TWE) project is a 3000 MW bipolar HVDC system with dedicated metallic 
return (DMR). The link will connect to the 500 kV AC system in Wyoming (WY) via two 345/500 kV 
auto-transformers to the 345 kV AC system in Utah (UT) near to the Intermountain substation. 
Purpose of the application is to bring bulk power from the Chokecherry and Sierra Madre (CCSM) Wind 
Energy Project in WY to the UT converter station. The power will be transmitted further south to load 
centers in California via the existing Intermountain HVDC link as well as a new 500kV series-
compensated AC line.  
 
The purpose of the GC studies in the FEED phase is to check and validate the new AC network data 
provided by the Employer, repeat the MIIF screening study at WY side, as well as the stability study 
for the whole project.

Pos 30: Stability, Modulation and Frequency control study 
The fast controllability of the HVDC PLUS enables the possibility to improve the power system stability 
using special modulation functions. The design of the required modulation functions of the HVDC PLUS 
and the interaction of the HVDC PLUS with the AC system are the main tasks of the stability study. 
 
2.3.1 
Scope 
The objectives of the study on "Stability, Modulation and Frequency Control" are: 
• Evaluate the stability of the interconnected transmission system for system faults and other 
relevant contingencies. Stability in this context means the rotor angle stability of generators 
(synchronism), the stability of voltage and frequency in the power systems, and the stable 
operation of the HVDC PLUS link.

(synchronism), the stability of voltage and frequency in the power systems, and the stable 
operation of the HVDC PLUS link. 
• To investigate the need, and if so, to demonstrate the effectiveness of possible supplementary 
functions (such as frequency control, AC voltage control, runbacks/runups) of the HVDC PLUS 
system.

1 Introduction 
Lanwin 4 is an offshore platform operated by TenneT and located in the North Sea, Germany.  In this 
platform, a 2GW-convoy standard design collects offshore wind power in the North Sea and transfer 
it to an onshore converter in Wilhelmshaven by bipole HVDC configuration with DMR. 
The following offer is created based on the customer's network data in PowerFactory, in accordance 
with “2GW_WHAV_Netzmodell_2031_V1.pfd”.

2.2 
Pos 20 SSTI part 1 Screening  
2.2.1 
Scope 
The goal of this study is to evaluate the possibility of Sub-Synchronous Torsional Interaction (SSTI) 
between synchronous generators and the Lanwin 4 HVDC PLUS. The study ensures that there is no 
detrimental interaction between the HVDC PLUS converter controls and the generator-shaft-systems 
in the sub-synchronous frequency range.  
The objective of the screening study (SSTI Part 1) is the following: 
• 
To identify specific thermal generators, for which SSTI between the generator and the HVDC 
PLUS converter is probable, in a screening study based on the calculation of Unit Interaction 
Factors (UIF), as defined by EPRI.

hermal generators, for which SSTI between the generator and the HVDC 
PLUS converter is probable, in a screening study based on the calculation of Unit Interaction 
Factors (UIF), as defined by EPRI.  
 
2.2.2 
Methodology 
For the evaluation of the risk of SSTI between a generator and a converter station, the following study 
methods are applied: 
• 
In the first step, the Unit Interaction Factors (UIF) for all generators under consideration is 
determined (“screening study”). This is a simple method to check the probability of SSTI. The 
output of the screening study is a list of generators which shall be analysed in a detailed study 
in time domain due to high UIF values.  
• 
The screening study relies on stationary short-circuit calculations. The HVDC modelling does 
not have influence on the screening study results. HVDC or FACTS devices are considered to 
have no short circuit contribution according to IEC 60919-3.

based on definition from CIGRE [*]. The assessment of the results will be in line with the 
recommendations of VGB white paper [**] and Cigre Guideline [*].

February 2021

2.3 
Pos 30: MIIF Screening Study 
2.3.1 
Scope 
A Screening Study for assessing potential interaction with other power electronic equipment in the AC 
network will be performed in accordance with CIGRÉ WG B4.41 or other methods as part of the 
engineering process. Additional interaction factors can be discussed and agreed between the 
Customer and the Contractor. 
 
2.3.2 
Methodology 
• 
Calculation of the Multi Infeed Interaction Factor (MIIF) in an RMS-Tool to estimate the 
potential risk of control interaction between different devices in the power system.  
• 
Calculation of the Power weighted Multi Infeed Interaction Factor (PWMIIF) in an RMS-Tool 
to estimate the potential risk of control interaction between different devices in the power 
system.

.  
• 
Calculation of the Power weighted Multi Infeed Interaction Factor (PWMIIF) in an RMS-Tool 
to estimate the potential risk of control interaction between different devices in the power 
system.  
• 
Calculation of the Multi-Infeed effective short circuit ratio (MIESCR) to estimate the potential 
risk of control interaction with power electronic devices 
• 
Devices connected to bus bars with significantly high MIIF, PWMIIF, and MIESCR values show 
a potential risk of interactions and will be considered for further detailed investigations.  
• 
Thus MIIF, PWMIIF, and MIESCR values give a useful indication about the size of the AC 
network (depth of impact) to be covered in the following interaction studies.

1 Introduction 
Balwin 3 is an offshore platform operated by TenneT and located in the North Sea, Germany.  In this 
platform, a 2GW-convoy standard design collects offshore wind power in the North Sea and transfer 
it to an onshore converter in Wilhelmshaven by bipole HVDC configuration with DMR.  
This document outlines the deviations from the customer specifications for the Balwin 3 HVDC 2GW 
Bipole project. These deviations have been carefully evaluated to ensure compliance with 
performance requirements while maintaining system reliability and operational efficiency. Detailed 
justifications for each deviation are provided in the following sections.

2.1 G-SPE.00.050-2GW-A01_Annex_B.300 (dated July 2022) 
2.1.1 
Section 6.12 Power Oscillation damping (POD function) 
The Contractor shall conduct a detailed technical assessment to determine the necessity of 
implementing Power Oscillation Damping through reactive power modulation (POD-Q) for the 
Employer-delivered (AC) power system. Where such implementation is deemed technically justified, 
the Contractor shall evaluate the potential effectiveness of the POD-Q function in enhancing the 
damping of electromechanical oscillations within the frequency range of 0.1 Hz to 2 Hz. 
The Contractor cannot guarantee that the POD-Q function will achieve uniform damping 
enhancement across the entire specified frequency spectrum.

ations within the frequency range of 0.1 Hz to 2 Hz. 
The Contractor cannot guarantee that the POD-Q function will achieve uniform damping 
enhancement across the entire specified frequency spectrum. The damping performance of the POD-
Q function is contingent upon a range of factors, including, but not limited to, the control system 
design parameters, the tuning of the POD controller, and the dynamic behavior of the interconnected 
power system—particularly the system’s observability and controllability at the point of common 
coupling (PCC). 
Consequently, the effectiveness of the POD-Q function may exhibit significant variability due to the 
electrical configuration, network topology, and operational conditions of the surrounding grid 
infrastructure, all of which are beyond the Contractor’s scope of responsibility and control.

1.3 Scope of Work 
a) Changeover of 2 top circuits to HVDC and Maximum allowable DC voltage: 
For the purposes of this preliminary study, it is reasonable to assume that the tower structure 
and conductors (including the bundle size and number of subconductors) are not altered. It is 
also assumed that the AC insulators will be replaced by DC insulators of the same length and 
appropriate creepage distance.  
The objective of this task is to estimate the maximum transferable power once the transmission 
line is converted to HVDC. With the conductors remaining unchanged, the maximum 
transferable power is mainly dependent on the maximum DC voltage allowed, as the DC 
current can be only about 1% higher than rms AC current.

text:
DC. With the conductors remaining unchanged, the maximum 
transferable power is mainly dependent on the maximum DC voltage allowed, as the DC 
current can be only about 1% higher than rms AC current. The maximum allowed AC voltage 
depends on multiple factors, namely the conductor to tower, conductor-to-conductor and mid-
span ground clearances, electric field strength at the ground level, ion current density and 
electric field gradient limits. The electric fields are in turn dependent on the arrangement of 
the positive and negative poles on the tower. The presence of the double circuit 110kV 
conductors on the same tower also impacts the electric field strength and gradients.  
For this preliminary study, SEGC will calculate the voltage limitation due to the air clearances, 
surface gradient, ionic current and static electric field at the edge of the right of way. Further 
detailed calculation of the radio interference, audible noise, corona losses etc.

b) EMT Interference Study: 
The presence of HVDC and AC conductors in close vicinity for almost the entire length of the 
line has several impacts that need to be studied. These include the induced AC voltage and 
currents in the DC line in steady state, the impact of DC faults on AC protection and vice versa, 
and the impact of AC and DC conductors touching each other. All these issues should be 
studied and addressed by the HVDC converter manufacturer at the design stage. At this 
preliminary stage it is sufficient to study the AC current and voltage induced in the DC lines. 
The study will be performed using PSCAD electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation tool 
which allows accurate geometrical presentation of the AC and DC conductors. The HVDC 
converters will be modelled by generic models.

2. Scope of Work 
Siemens requested a quote from TGS to perform the following tasks: 
1. Tower re-design for changeover of 2 top circuits to HVDC – TNSP will provide 5 x .dwg files as 
input and have already provided a snapshot of geometry and span lengths.   
2. Switching impulse calculation that determines max allowable DC voltage for given power levels.   
3. Interference studies (electromagnetic coupling and interaction studies of the AC and DC lines on 
the same tower) in EMT as an optional section.

text:
le DC voltage 
For the purposes of this preliminary study, it is reasonable to assume that the tower structure and 
conductors (including the bundle size and number of subconductors) are not altered. It is also assumed 
that the AC insulators will be replaced by DC insulators of the same length and appropriate creepage 
distance.  
The objective of this task is to estimate the maximum transferable power once the transmission line is 
converted to HVDC. With the conductors remaining unchanged, the maximum transferable power is 
mainly dependent on the maximum DC voltage allowed, as the DC current can be only about 1% higher 
than rms AC current. The maximum allowed AC voltage depends on multiple factors, namely the 
conductor to tower, conductor-to-conductor and mid-span ground clearances, electric field strength at the 
ground level, ion current density and electric field gradient limits.

conductor to tower, conductor-to-conductor and mid-span ground clearances, electric field strength at the 
ground level, ion current density and electric field gradient limits. The electric fields are in turn dependent 
on the arrangement of the positive and negative poles on the tower. The presence of the double circuit 
110kV conductors on the same tower also impacts the electric field strength and gradients.  
For this preliminary study TGS will calculate the voltage limitation due to the air clearances, surface 
gradient, ionic current and static electric field at the edge of the right of way. Further detailed calculation

2.2 
Optional Task 2 – EMT Interference studies 
The presence of HVDC and AC conductors in close vicinity for almost the entire length of the line has 
several impacts that need to be studied. These include the induced AC voltage and currents in the DC 
line in steady state, the impact of DC faults on AC protection and vice versa, and the impact of AC and 
DC conductors touching each other. All these issues should be studied and addressed by the HVDC 
converter manufacturer at the design stage. At this preliminary stage it is sufficient to study the AC current 
and voltage induced in the DC lines. The study will be performed using PSCAD electromagnetic transient 
(EMT) simulation tool which allows accurate geometrical presentation of the AC and DC conductors. The 
HVDC converters will be modeled by generic models. AC lines are assumed to be carrying their rated 
currents.

NTS FOR PROJECT EXECUTION AND OPERATIONAL PHASE 
All studies and simulation models shall be created meeting the given requirement before the 
converter is installed and shall be submitted to 50Hertz.  
 
The Contractor shall provide a list which includes all study outline reports, study reports and models 
including delivery dates of the documents which needs to be agreed with 50Hertz. Further, the 
Contractor shall link the respective report with the applicable requirements in this TRN. 
 
The Contractor shall supply the models together with the study report in which they are used. If 
necessary, 50hertz can request a preliminary version of the model and share it with the relevant third 
party to perform the required simulation study with vendor-specific detailed models.

the converter system and the AC network representation, if applicable.

6.3.1 MODEL OF CONVERTER 
A model of the converter shall be provided in order to perform instantaneous value simulations (EMT 
simulations). Every power electronics system consists of components that fall into one of the 
following three groups for simulation purposes: 
 
• 
Power unit:  
The power unit comprises electrical, magnetic and mechanical components such as transformers, 
converter hardware (including semiconductors, filters, sensors/transducers) and switchgear.

ower unit:  
The power unit comprises electrical, magnetic and mechanical components such as transformers, 
converter hardware (including semiconductors, filters, sensors/transducers) and switchgear. 
• 
Control hardware:  
The term ‘control hardware’ covers all hardware that is not located in the power unit and is used, for 
example, for the control, regulation or protection of the system. These can be digital systems such as 
industrial PCs or electronic assemblies with microprocessors, digital signal processors or FPGAs. 
Analog controls also fall within this group. 
• 
Control software:  
The control software group essentially includes the software run on the associated control hardware 
and that realises the desired control function. This applies, for example, to the software for 
controlling the converters or the software for generating the pulses for the active semiconductor 
valves.

8.4.1 STUDY OVERVIEW 
The Contractor shall submit a study overview report to 50Hertz no later than two months before the 
start of DPS. Before the DPS can start, 50Hertz will have approved the study overview report. The 
Contractor shall add a test matrix for the DPS to the study overview report that considers the 
boundary conditions. The test matrix shall list all simulations and tests as well as the boundary 
conditions and detailed information about the test set-up.  
 
The Dynamic Performance Study shall be conducted in three stages: 
1. 
A brief demonstration of the dynamic performance of the converter system for a small 
number of representative events. It is the goal of the initial study to demonstrate the general 
performance of the converter system in the earliest design phase. 
2. 
A detailed demonstration of performance at an early stage in the control design.

dynamic performance of the converter system shall be compared to the requirements in the 
relevant TRN [1, 2, 3, 4]. It is not needed to fulfil all requirements when the study is 
executed. Rather, it is the goal to clearly reveal the gaps between requirements and asset 
performance, to show the general feasibility and to define action items to close these gaps.  
3. 
A performance demonstration with a well-developed control design. Before the Contractor 
starts this study, the Contractor shall have closed all gaps identified previously. At the end of 
the study, the converter system shall show full compliance to the requirements.

 TRANSIENT TORQUE GAIN ANALYSIS 
Transient torque gain analysis shall investigate the influence of the converter on SSTI in the event of 
supply failures, using EMT simulations in the time domain. 
Such analyses shall simulate a three-pole short circuit in the base case with and without a connected 
converter and calculate the transient torque for each individual mass of the shaft assembly as a result 
of the fault. The resulting transient torque or rotational speeds focusing on the natural frequencies of 
the shaft assembly in question, shall be compared for both cases. Post-processing (e.g., FFT for 
extracting the signals at the resonance frequencies) shall supplement the evaluation based on the 
plots from the time domain simulations.

The Contractor shall calculate and deliver the converter voltage emissions in the sub-synchronous

the mechanical shaft system of the relevant power plants. Then, the voltage emissions for a frequency 
range of ±1.5 Hz around each resonance frequency shall be calculated. The Contractor shall calculate 
the voltage emissions insteps of 0.1 Hz in the frequency range.

operating modes.

1 Introduction 
Lanwin6 is an offshore platform operated by 50 Hertz and located in the North Sea, Germany. The 
interconnection with the German transmission grid will be performed with a 2 GW capacity. 
This document outlines the deviations from the customer specifications for the Lanwin6 HVDC 2GW 
Bipole project. These deviations have been carefully evaluated to ensure compliance with 
performance requirements while maintaining system reliability and operational efficiency. Detailed 
justifications for each deviation are provided in the following sections.

2.2.1 
Scope 
The goal of this study is to evaluate the possibility of Sub-Synchronous Torsional Interaction (SSTI) 
between synchronous generators and the Lanwin 6 HVDC PLUS. The study ensures that there is no 
detrimental interaction between the HVDC PLUS converter controls and the generator-shaft-systems 
in the sub-synchronous frequency range.  
The objective of the screening study (SSTI Part 1) is the following: 
• 
To identify specific thermal generators, for which SSTI between the generator and the HVDC 
PLUS converter is probable, in a screening study based on the calculation of Unit Interaction 
Factors (UIF), as defined by EPRI.

2.2.2 
Methodology 
For the evaluation of the risk of SSTI between a generator and a converter station, the following study 
methods are applied: 
• 
In the first step, the Unit Interaction Factors (UIF) for all generators under consideration is 
determined (“screening study”). This is a simple method to check the probability of SSTI. The 
output of the screening study is a list of generators which shall be analysed in a detailed study 
in time domain due to high UIF values.

not have influence on the screening study results. HVDC or FACTS devices are considered to

2.11 Pos 80-c: Onshore & Offshore Harmonic Stability  
 
2.11.1 Scope 
The purpose of this study is to investigate the harmonic stability of the Lanwin 6 converter station. 
This is done using impedance-based analysis. Harmonic stability is confirmed using the Nyquist 
criterion. The analysis is done in the frequency range of 10 Hz to 2500 Hz. 
 
2.11.2 Methodology 
For the onshore & offshore harmonic stability study, the software MATLAB is used both to construct 
the harmonic model of the HVDC converters and to conduct the stability analysis. 
The harmonic stability can be analyzed at each system connection point, or each point at which two 
subsystems connect.

e harmonic model of the HVDC converters and to conduct the stability analysis. 
The harmonic stability can be analyzed at each system connection point, or each point at which two 
subsystems connect. The harmonic stability is determined based on the ratio of the input and output 
impedance at each of these connection points. The stability of the connection is determined by the 
Nyquist stability criterion of the ratio of the input and output impedance.  
Because harmonic stability investigations are not yet state-of-the-art, this section will present the 
theory behind the methodology, as well as the planned steps in the investigation. 
The fundamental concept in impedance-based stability analysis is centered around the idea of 
electrical coupling. When two components are electrically connected, their combined behavior 
transcends their individual characteristics, resulting in a transfer function that represents the entire 
system.

al coupling. When two components are electrically connected, their combined behavior 
transcends their individual characteristics, resulting in a transfer function that represents the entire 
system. Consequently, the interconnection of two stable systems can sometimes lead to instability. 
To address the impact of electrical coupling, the impedance-based analysis method examines the 
point of interaction between the two subsystems, which is where the coupling takes place. 
To illustrate the method, consider the example of a voltage-source inverter. A simple circuit diagram 
of a system containing a voltage-source inverter connected to a load is shown in Figure 2-3.

B2- Particular Technical Requirements - HVDC 
1 
General 
This specification provides the minimum functional and technical requirements for the Converter 
Stations of the Sarawak-Singapore HVDC power transmission system. 
The Contractor shall carry out detailed design, engineering, testing and commissioning to 
demonstrate and document full compliance with the Project requirements and minimum perfor-
mance and Grid Code requirements. 
The detailed design and engineering to be undertaken by the Contractor shall include all the 
studies and surveys deemed necessary for the design, permitting, manufacture, installation, test-
ing, commissioning and safe operation of the Singapore and Sarawak Converter Stations.

The Contractor shall carry out all studies deemed necessary to prove that the Converter Stations 
will be able to deliver the minimum performance levels, meet the Project and Grid Code require-
ments and operate safely and efficiently at any time along the envisaged service lifetime. It shall 
be noted that well-established grid codes, i.e. ENTSO-E Network Code and GB Grid Code are

enough specific information about HVDC connection to the AC network at the moment.

Cable Spare Parts Building 
means the building where the spare AC cables (supplied by the Contractor) and spare DC land 
cables (supplied by others), and other parts and materials (required to maintain the AC cable and 
DC land cable sections) shall be stored. 
Control Building 
means the building, located between the Equipment Halls, which accommodates the majority of 
the HVDC control and protection equipment, major parts of the auxiliary systems (like converter 
cooling, auxiliary power etc.) and provides offices and service areas for the operators and the 
maintenance personnel.

Scope of Supply 
4.1 
Scope Overview 
This document covers the design, manufacture, supply, installation, commissioning and trial op-
eration of the Sarawak-Singapore HVDC power transmission system. 
The HVDC system shall be 2 x 900 MW HVDC Links, with symmetrical monopole configuration in 
voltage sourced converter (VSC) technology and MMC topology. The rated DC voltage shall be 
± 320 kV and the DC operating voltage shall be ± 320 kV at the rectifier station. 
The converter station in Sarawak (the Sarawak Converter Station) shall be connected to the Sara-
wak high voltage network via the Tondong substation (the Sarawak Substation), which is approx-
imately 50 m away. The Sarawak Converter Station shall be a complete  500 kV GIS for connection 
to existing grid 500kV Switchyard.

4.4 
HVDC Operation and Monitoring Basic Requirements  
The HVDC system shall be controlled remotely from one of the two remote control centers or by 
the local operator at either converter station. The normal operating mode will be active power 
control by active power setpoint at a selected measurement point (AC/DC at rectifier or inverter). 
Selection of one control location for active power reference scheduling will automatically disable 
the other control locations.

formance of the HVDC protection system. This study shall identify the protection devices, their

protection design phase, that a minimum of two different protection functions shall be capable 
of clearing the fault. The Contractor shall demonstrate that damage to equipment is minimized 
by proper coordination of protection functions.

electronic devices in the Employer’s and neighboring grids could have an interaction with the

change.

8.2 
Active Power Control 
The HVDC System shall provide active power over the full range of converter capability within the 
converter rating documented in Section 9. During normal operation of both symmetrical mono-
poles, the active power range of the converter shall be 2 x 600 MW. The HVDC system shall 
automatically distribute active power setpoint between the poles. It shall be possible to override 
the automatically distributed setpoint, i.e. to enable ramping down of one pole to zero MW in 
preparation for planned maintenance. During single monopole operation, the active power range 
of the single monopole shall be increased to its rated active power (900 MW).

preparation for planned maintenance. During single monopole operation, the active power range 
of the single monopole shall be increased to its rated active power (900 MW). 
The active power control range shall be continuous, i.e. with no dead-band either side of 0 MW. 
The setpoints of the active power to be transmitted shall be adjustable in steps of at least 10 MW. 
In steady state conditions, the magnitude of the error between set-point and measured value for 
active power shall not exceed 0.5% of the nominal DC power rating of the converter. 
The active power gradient must be adjustable in the range between 1 MW/min and the maximum 
technically possible gradient, but at least 10 MW/min. The active power gradient must be main-
tained with a maximum error of 1% - related to the set value. 
DC voltage at the rectifier Converter Station shall be controlled to the operating DC voltage of

verter capability within the converter rating documented in Section 9. The HVDC system shall 
automatically distribute reactive power setpoint between the poles. It shall be possible to override 
the automatically distributed setpoint, i.e. to enable ramping down of one pole to zero Mvar in

Reactive power control shall be provided for all AC system conditions, coupled/decoupled oper-

Dynamic Voltage Support 
The HVDC-System shall be capable of providing continuous dynamic voltage support at the PCC 
of each converter station, especially during fault ride through. Dynamic voltage control shall op-
erate in parallel with the reactive power control function for slower voltage changes as specified 
in Section 8.3. 
The following general requirement shall apply to dynamic voltage support: 
▪ operation in the positive and negative phase sequence systems 
▪ The HVDC System shall be capable of injecting a current equal to 100% rated current in each 
phase for dynamic voltage support. 
The performance requirement for dynamic voltage support shall be further refined during the 
detailed design stage in coordination with the Employer based on similar requirements such as 
the GB Grid Code (Section ECC.6.3.16).

The HVDC System shall provide fast-acting emergency power control to support the transmission 
system operators, whereby the HVDC responds to pre-defined emergency power control actions 
(e.g. reduce power by a predefined MW amount and ramp) triggered by automatic signals hard-
wired binary signals received from the transmission system operators (e.g. after detection of rel-
evant contingency). It shall be possible to enable / disable the emergency power control actions.

HVDC system shall respond to multiple emergency power control signals sequentially, taking into 
account prioritization of actions in case of conflicting control actions.

Black Start Capability 
The HVDC System shall provide black start functionality for both sides of the Converter Station. 
In black start operation, the HVDC system shall be used to restore voltage to a network with no 
other sources of generation and to remain in operation during the restoration of other network 
components such as transmission lines, transformers, load and generators.  
The specific requirements regarding availability, number of consecutive black starts, frequency 
setpoint, voltage ramping, active/reactive power loading, load dumping and operational proce-
dures shall be coordinated with the transmission system. 
Diesel generators (or other facilities to provide auxiliary power to the sub-systems necessary for 
black start) shall be provided.

8.17 
HVDC Cable Discharge 
Following planned and unplanned outages of the HVDC System, the DC cable shall be discharged 
within a maximum duration of 3 minutes to a voltage level at which restart of the HVDC system 
is possible. 
The Contractor shall describe faster solutions including updated equipment schemes and single 
line diagrams. The changes in the equipment scope shall be limited to the implementation of fast 
DC switches. No DC breakers shall be used. 
8.18 
Loss Evaluation 
The Contractor shall guarantee the total Converter Station losses at 100 % rated power.

10.4.10 HVDC Disturbance Recorder 
The Contractor shall provide stand-alone, HVDC dedicated systems for sequence of event record-
ing and transient fault recording.  
The sequence of event recorder (SER) shall record all alarms, indications and operator inputs (for 
example set-point changes) with a time resolution suitable for determining the order in which 
events occur of at least 1ms or better. The SER shall be in continuous operation, i.e. not only 
recording by triggering by disturbances. The SER shall also record all main AC and DC analogue 
quantities at a regular interval of sixty seconds or faster. Archiving historical SER data shall be 
provided.

ing grade with Underwriters Laboratory classification equal to or better than UL94 V-0 for vertical

alent classification).

10.9 
AC Filter Reactors 
The reactors for harmonic filters shall not contain any moving parts and shall be constructed 
generally in accordance with IEC 60076-6. The insulation shall be Class B and the maximum per-
mitted winding temperature rise shall be 70°C. 
The reactors shall be of single-phase type and shall be supplied complete including all required 
insulators, supports and structure. 
The reactors shall be designed not to exceed the following hottest spot temperature for the re-
spective loading conditions and specified maximum ambient dry bulb temperature: 
▪ continuous rating 115°C 
 
The Contractor may propose a higher temperature class insulation, but this shall be reliable, and 
the hottest spot temperature rise shall be with more safety margin than for Class B insulation. 
The reactors shall be provided with lifting eyes to facilitate rapid erection and replacement of the 
reactors.

The reactors shall be provided with lifting eyes to facilitate rapid erection and replacement of the 
reactors. Off load taps shall be provided, if required, only for initial tuning of the filters. 
The air-cooled, dry type, air insulated reactors shall be suitable for outdoor mounting and shall 
be mounted so that any mutual coupling between phases or between filters does not adversely 
affect the performance of the filter, and adequate precautions shall be taken to prevent over-
heating of any magnetic material located in the magnetic field of the reactor. 
The rated voltage (rms) of the filter reactor shall be the arithmetic sum of the rms voltage of 
fundamental frequency and at each harmonic across the reactor. The current rating (rms) of the 
filter reactor shall be the square root of the sum of the squared values of the rms currents at

Voltage Rating 
The voltage rating (rms) of an AC filter or shunt capacitor shall be based on the arithmetic sum 
of the rms voltages at fundamental frequency and at each harmonic.  
The voltage rating shall be based on continuous duty or equivalent requirements derived from 
temporary duty, whichever is the greatest.  
The voltage rating of a capacitor unit shall be equal to the rated voltage of the constituent ca-
pacitor bank divided by the number of units in series.  
Current Rating 
The current rating (rms) of an AC filter or shunt capacitor shall be defined as the arithmetic sum 
of the rms currents at fundamental frequency and at each harmonic.  
The current rating shall be based on continuous duty or equivalent requirements derived from 
temporary duty, whichever is the greatest.

1. Project Description 
1.1 
Introduction 
a. 
The Sarawak Consortium consisting of Sembcorp Industries and Sarawak Energy Berhad, referred to 
collectively as the Principal, are currently developing a high-voltage direct current (HVDC) interconnection 
between Sarawak (Tondong) and Singapore (Changi East).   
b. 
This power import facility is designed as a grid-to-grid HVDC interconnection, linking the Sarawak 
transmission network with the Singapore Transmission Network.  
c. 
The Principal has proposed to export up to 1.4 Gigawatt (GW) of renewable energy from Sarawak, Malaysia 
to Singapore via an HVDC transmission scheme with submarine cables and partially HVDC overhead lines 
at the Sarawak onshore area. 
d. 
On the Sarawak side, the HVDC submarine cables land on the coastline, proceeding to a transition yard 
near Sampadi.

marine cables and partially HVDC overhead lines

d. 
On the Sarawak side, the HVDC submarine cables land on the coastline, proceeding to a transition yard 
near Sampadi. From this juncture, it will be routed to an HVDC overhead line (OHL) that extends overland 
for approximately 40 kilometres, leading directly to the Sarawak converter station adjacent to the Tondong 
500/275 kV HVAC substation.  
e. 
The designated route for the submarine cable stretches from Sampadi to Changi Aviation Park in Singapore, 
covering a total length of roughly 750 kilometres. 
f.

a. 
The HVDC system includes two independent and parallel 900 MW rated HVDC symmetrical monopoles 
(SMPs).  
b. 
The maximum import capacity of the system is limited to 1.4 GW.

c. 
The two SMPs shall be independent of one another. The performance of each SMP shall be considered

possibility of a switching operation being performed that will or has the potential to result in equipment 
damage or risk to the safety of personnel.

witnessed and approved by the Principal, the Transmission Licensee and the Power System Operator. 
c.

Any high voltage isolators that are not rated for load-break cannot be opened while there is 
load/current present. 
ii. 
Any high voltage isolator may not be closed onto a section of the high voltage circuit with a 
closed earth switch. 
iii. 
Any earth switch cannot be closed onto an energised section of the high voltage circuit.

2 RMS interaction study 
2.1 
Study objective with reference to 4GTSO innovation partnership 
In addition to the grid connection requirements of a P2P HVDC, MTDC have, due to their increased 
complexity an increased level of interactions with grid assets within the MTDC System and in the AC-
grid sections surrounding the converter stations. 
Therefore, additional studies shall be conducted to evaluate the interaction between the MTDC system 
and other electrically close converter stations and their connected DC systems. 
Due to the intended size of the simulation model, the study shall be conducted in RMS.

action between the MTDC system 
and other electrically close converter stations and their connected DC systems. 
Due to the intended size of the simulation model, the study shall be conducted in RMS. 
All modular construction stages based on the project specific sequences are to be considered for the 
proof of robustness against changes in the DC configuration 
The study shall investigate: 
a) Effects of the MTDC System on the AC grid surrounding converter stations and close 
HVDC systems, 
b) Change of control parameters in the MTDC system 
c) Change of control modes in the MTDC system 
d) Effects of the MTDC System on remote converter stations (DC and AC side) of electrically 
close HVDC systems. 
e) Effects due to the parallel structure of HVDC Systems to the AC transmission grid. Such 
as:

behaviour of one converter station in the MTDC system when effects of a grid 
event on another converter station of the same MTDC reach this converter station 
via the AC and the DC path.

coordinated between manufacturer and TSOs.

2 RMS interaction study 
2.1 
Study objective with reference to 4GTSO innovation partnership 
In addition to the grid connection requirements of a P2P HVDC, MTDC have, due to their increased 
complexity an increased level of interactions with grid assets within the MTDC System and in the AC-
grid sections surrounding the converter stations. 
Therefore, additional studies shall be conducted to evaluate the interaction between the MTDC system 
and other electrically close converter stations and their connected DC systems. 
Due to the intended size of the simulation model, the study shall be conducted in RMS.

action between the MTDC system 
and other electrically close converter stations and their connected DC systems. 
Due to the intended size of the simulation model, the study shall be conducted in RMS. 
All modular construction stages based on the project specific sequences are to be considered for the 
proof of robustness against changes in the DC configuration 
The study shall investigate: 
a) Effects of the MTDC System on the AC grid surrounding converter stations and close 
HVDC systems, 
b) Change of control parameters in the MTDC system 
c) Change of control modes in the MTDC system 
d) Effects of the MTDC System on remote converter stations (DC and AC side) of electrically 
close HVDC systems. 
e) Effects due to the parallel structure of HVDC Systems to the AC transmission grid. Such 
as: 
I. 
behaviour of one converter station in the MTDC system when effects of a grid 
event on another converter station of the same MTDC reach this converter station 
via the AC and the DC path.

h 
as:

behaviour of one converter station in the MTDC system when effects of a grid 
event on another converter station of the same MTDC reach this converter station 
via the AC and the DC path. 
Excluded from the study are: 
f) 
Transient effects such as current clipping which are covered in the dynamic performance 
study. 
g) Sub-/supersynchronous oscillations as covered in chapter 3 
h) Harmonic effects

Prior to the study a pre-evaluation shall be conducted in coordination with the TSOs to coordinate this

be evaluated in RMS and must therefore be investigated in the DPS study. 
The development of models, provision of models from the TSOs, study schedule and review shall be 
coordinated between manufacturer and TSOs.

1 Introduction 
 
The following document represents the technical proposal from Siemens Energy (SE) Grid 
Consulting for the development of the AC network harmonic impedance areas seen at the 
points of connection of the Tyrrhenian Link HVDC converters. The analysis shall be carried out 
for each integer harmonic from the 2nd to the 50th to aid the design of the new HVDC converter 
stations. 
 
The following grid elements shall be considered as part of the grid electronic model: 
• 
Transmission lines and cables 
• 
Power plants (both conventional and renewable) 
• 
Loads 
• 
Shunt capacitor banks and reactors 
• 
Power transformers 
• 
Load flow conditions (operating scenarios) 
 
Appropriate mathematical models of the electrical system, focusing on frequency-dependent 
representations of lines, cables, transformers, generators, load

oad flow conditions (operating scenarios) 
 
Appropriate mathematical models of the electrical system, focusing on frequency-dependent 
representations of lines, cables, transformers, generators, loads, power semiconductor 
converters, capacitor banks and shunt reactors are used to model the equipment in the

1 Introduction 
This technical proposal outlines the detailed scope, methodologies, deliverables, tools, and 
stakeholder interactions for the Wyoming Intertie (WyTie) HVDC Planning Study.  
In this document, the Client/Employer is referred to as Grid United. The Consultant/Contractor is 
referred to as Siemens Energy Grid Consulting. 
 
1.1 Project description 
 
Wyoming Intertie (WyTie) HVDC Project is a proposed 1,800 MW, 320 kV, HVDC Interconnection Tie 
between the Aeolus 500 kV substation in Carbon County, Wyoming (WECC) and the Laramie River  
345 kV Substation in Platte County, Wyoming (SPP). Geographical depiction of the proposed WyTie  
HVDC line is shown in Figure 1-1.   
As per the feasibility study conducted by the client, the preliminary rating of 1500 MW HVDC intertie 
is proposed.

HVDC line is shown in Figure 1-1.

is proposed. As major transmission upgrades at and near the WyTie point of interconnection (POI) at 
Laremie have been approved by SPP. The client will conduct further feasibility study on a proposed 
rating of 1800 MW.

3.2 POS 20 Preliminary PSS/E HVDC model development 
3.2.1 Scope 
The Contractor will develop a preliminary HVDC model in PSS®E, intended for steady-state analysis 
and for power system stability studies, particularly focusing on electro-mechanical dynamics.  
In RMS domain studies, the AC power system is typically represented by the positive sequence. 
Therefore, the HVDC VSC model will represent the converter performance for the positive sequence. 
All functions related to unbalanced operation is not part of the model implementation. In addition, 
dynamics of very fast converter control loops operating in the transient timescale cannot be 
implemented in an RMS model.

unbalanced operation is not part of the model implementation. In addition, 
dynamics of very fast converter control loops operating in the transient timescale cannot be 
implemented in an RMS model. The purpose of this model is to demonstrate preliminary dynamic 
performance for voltage and frequency stability functions at WyTie POIs.  
Methodology: 
In power system stability studies, the slower dynamics such as electro-mechanical oscillations can be 
captured using a fundamental frequency model such as an RMS model.  Therefore, the stability model 
is valid for the use of investigations related to the following phenomena: 
• 
Classical stability studies in large, interconnected power systems 
o Rotor angle stability of generators 
o Voltage stability in the power system 
o Frequency stability of the power system 
• 
These phenomena can be studied in the electro-mechanical time frame assuming symmetrical 
operation.

Due to the fact, that the HVDC VSC model will have small time constants in the control loops, a fine 
time step increment of around 1 ms is required. The de facto time step of the models will be defined 
based on the finally implemented control concept and parameters.

To demonstrate the stability of the interconnected transmission system for system faults and

generators (synchronism), the stability of voltage and frequency in the power systems, and 
the stable operation of the HVDC VSC link.

The SSTI screening studies will be performed for both POIs of the WyTie HVDC. 
4.1.1 Scope 
The goal of this study is to evaluate the possibility of Sub-Synchronous Torsional Interaction (SSTI) 
between synchronous generators and WyTie HVDC PLUS. The study ensures that there is no 
detrimental interaction between the HVDC PLUS converter controls and the generator-shaft-systems 
in the sub-synchronous frequency range.  
The objective of the screening study (SSTI Part 1) is the following: 
• To identify specific thermal generators, for which SSTI between the generator and the HVDC 
PLUS converter is probable, in a screening study based on the calculation of Unit Interaction 
Factors (UIF), as defined by [R03].

Factors (UIF), as defined by [R03].  
• Methodologies highlighted in the latest EPRI recommendations [R03] and Cigre TB 909 [R04] 
will be used for this screening study. 
 
4.1.2 Methodology 
For the evaluation of the risk of SSTI between a generator and a converter station, the following study 
methods are applied: 
1. Synchronous generation units are first selected and grouped where appropriate.  
o Note, that synchronous units connected at a single bus that is of the same fuel type 
will be treated as a single unit for this study with an MVA rating equal to the sum of 
the individual machine ratings. I.e.: gas turbines of the same rating are grouped as a 
single unit.

In case of hydro units the high value of the generator rotor inertia in relation 
to the inertias of the turbine effectively shields the rotor mechanical system, 
making the excitation of torsional oscillations through generator disturbances 
highly unlikely.

Moreover, the viscous waterwheel damping makes the inherent damping of

1 OVERVIEW 
This document details the technical, performance and quality assurance requirements for furnishing, testing, and 
delivering one  (1) synchronous condenser system (SCS).  Provisions in this specification may be overruled by the 
project specific criteria of the technical data sheets in the appendices of this document.   
The SCS shall provide step-less automatic power factor correction without any switching transients and shall not 
generate harmonic currents or voltages or have adverse interactions with other electronic devices in the Owner’s 
substation.

For the purposes of this document, the firm, company, or vendor along with any designated sub-contractors shall be 
referred to as the “Contractor” for all pre-award and post-award activities of this project.  Xcel Energy and its 
appropriate operating affiliates shall be referred to as the “Owner” for the purpose of this specification. 
Use of this specification by the Contractor is restricted to Owner’s business only.  Distribution of this specification, 
in part or whole, to utilities or consultants outside of the Owner without written permission from Owner is strictly 
prohibited. 
This specification shall provide preliminary values for design and equipment ratings of the SCS.

This specification shall provide preliminary values for design and equipment ratings of the SCS.  The Contractor shall 
meet the requirements as outlined in this document and in accordance with the design specification values of the 
appendices.  The Contractor shall determine all final equipment ratings in their detailed design based on Contractor 
developed and Owner-approved system studies. 
This specification applies to synchronous condenser installations and to the major components of an installation that 
are required to form a complete system for the connection of synchronous condenser machines to a transmission 
system.

ous condenser installations and to the major components of an installation that 
are required to form a complete system for the connection of synchronous condenser machines to a transmission 
system.  These major components include synchronous machines, excitation system, lubrication system, cooling 
system, power transformer, surge arresters, circuit breakers, air-break disconnect switches, electrical equipment 
enclosure, and protection and control systems.  All components and equipment shall be new, of recent manufacture, 
and specifically for this SCS installation. 
This document specifies the design, engineering, manufacturing, factory testing, supply, construction, site testing, 
commissioning, operational competency sessions and placement into commercial service of a transmission-level SCS 
in the Owner’s transmission system.  All other relevant aspects of a transmission-level SCS project, including

The synchronous condenser starting sequence shall be as follows: 
1) A small pony motor (or static frequency converter) shall bring the synchronous condenser up to the network 
synchronous speed with the help of a variable speed drive.  Alternative starting systems may be proposed per 
the Contractor’s design. 
2) Excitation systems are fully connected, and the voltage and power factor regulators commence operation, 
based on the voltage and power factor reference. 
3) When synchronization is achieved between the network and synchronous condenser, the circuit breaker to 
the power system network is closed.  The synchronous condenser is not running on-line prior to this stage.

1 OVERVIEW 
This document details the technical, performance and quality assurance requirements for furnishing, testing, and 
delivering two (2) identical synchronous condenser systems (SCS).  Provisions in this specification may be overruled 
by the project specific criteria of the technical data sheets in the appendices of this document.   
The SCS shall provide step-less automatic power factor correction without any switching transients and shall not 
generate harmonic currents or voltages or have adverse interactions with other electronic devices in the Owner’s 
substation.
