For the purposes of this document, the firm, company, or vendor along with any designated sub-contractors shall be 
referred to as the “Contractor” for all pre-award and post-award activities of this project.  Xcel Energy and its 
appropriate operating affiliates shall be referred to as the “Owner” for the purpose of this specification. 
Use of this specification by the Contractor is restricted to Owner’s business only.  Distribution of this specification, 
in part or whole, to utilities or consultants outside of the Owner without written permission from Owner is strictly 
prohibited. 
This specification shall provide preliminary values for design and equipment ratings of the SCS.

This specification shall provide preliminary values for design and equipment ratings of the SCS.  The Contractor shall 
meet the requirements as outlined in this document and in accordance with the design specification values of the 
appendices.  The Contractor shall determine all final equipment ratings in their detailed design based on Contractor 
developed and Owner-approved system studies. 
This specification applies to synchronous condenser installations and to the major components of an installation that 
are required to form a complete system for the connection of synchronous condenser machines to a transmission 
system.

are required to form a complete system for the connection of synchronous condenser machines to a transmission

system, power transformer, surge arresters, circuit breakers, air-break disconnect switches, electrical equipment 
enclosure, and protection and control systems.  All components and equipment shall be new, of recent manufacture, 
and specifically for this SCS installation. 
This document specifies the design, engineering, manufacturing, factory testing, supply, construction, site testing, 
commissioning, operational competency sessions and placement into commercial service of a transmission-level SCS 
in the Owner’s transmission system.  All other relevant aspects of a transmission-level SCS project, including

This specification provides the Owner’s requirements for the installation of transmission level SCS to provide voltage 
or reactive power control.  The rotating machinery and auxiliary mechanical systems shall be designed for a forty-
year service life.  This specification and appendices, along with supplement specifications as detailed in Section 2 
shall comprise the technical requirements for the engineering, procurement, and installation of a SCS.

cooling systems, protection systems, control systems, step-up power transformer, surge arresters, synchronous 
condenser machine hall, indoor and outdoor switchgear.  
The contractor shall propose a SCS design that meets the requirements of this specification and should provide

condenser machine modules to achieve the required capacity or redundancy. 
The SCS control system shall be capable of voltage control based on the Owner’s transmission dispatch set point.  
Voltage control shall be measured and defined at the transmission PCC (point of common coupling), which can also

7.1.5 SYNCHRONOUS CONDENSER STARTING SEQUENCE 
The synchronous condenser starting sequence shall be as follows: 
1) A small pony motor (or static frequency converter) shall bring the synchronous condenser up to the network 
synchronous speed with the help of a variable speed drive. 
2) Excitation systems are fully connected, and the voltage and power factor regulators commence operation, 
based on the voltage and power factor reference. 
3) When synchronization is achieved between the network and synchronous condenser, the circuit breaker to 
the power system network is closed.  The synchronous condenser is not running on-line prior to this stage. 
4) After successful synchronization, the pony motor is de-energized and runs ideal with the synchronous 
condenser.

period, the SCS operation may be interrupted in accordance with the Contractor’s design and supply.

1 OVERVIEW 
This document details the technical, performance and quality assurance requirements for furnishing, testing, and 
delivering two (2) identical synchronous condenser systems (SCS).  Provisions in this specification may be overruled 
by the project specific criteria of the technical data sheets in the appendices of this document.   
The SCS shall provide step-less automatic power factor correction without any switching transients and shall not 
generate harmonic currents or voltages or have adverse interactions with other electronic devices in the Owner’s 
substation.

For the purposes of this document, the firm, company, or vendor along with any designated sub-contractors shall be 
referred to as the “Contractor” for all pre-award and post-award activities of this project.  Xcel Energy and its 
appropriate operating affiliates shall be referred to as the “Owner” for the purpose of this specification. 
Use of this specification by the Contractor is restricted to Owner’s business only.  Distribution of this specification, 
in part or whole, to utilities or consultants outside of the Owner without written permission from Owner is strictly 
prohibited. 
This specification shall provide preliminary values for design and equipment ratings of the SCS.

This specification shall provide preliminary values for design and equipment ratings of the SCS.  The Contractor shall 
meet the requirements as outlined in this document and in accordance with the design specification values of the 
appendices.  The Contractor shall determine all final equipment ratings in their detailed design based on Contractor 
developed and Owner-approved system studies. 
This specification applies to synchronous condenser installations and to the major components of an installation that 
are required to form a complete system for the connection of synchronous condenser machines to a transmission 
system.

ous condenser installations and to the major components of an installation that 
are required to form a complete system for the connection of synchronous condenser machines to a transmission 
system.  These major components include synchronous machines, excitation system, lubrication system, cooling 
system, power transformer, surge arresters, circuit breakers, air-break disconnect switches, electrical equipment 
enclosure, and protection and control systems.  All components and equipment shall be new, of recent manufacture, 
and specifically for this SCS installation. 
This document specifies the design, engineering, manufacturing, factory testing, supply, construction, site testing, 
commissioning, operational competency sessions and placement into commercial service of a transmission-level SCS 
in the Owner’s transmission system.  All other relevant aspects of a transmission-level SCS project, including 
commercial, are included in a separate document.

or reactive power control.  The rotating machinery and auxiliary mechanical systems shall be designed for a forty-
year service life.  This specification and appendices, along with supplement specifications as detailed in Section 2 
shall comprise the technical requirements for the engineering, procurement, and installation of a SCS.

7.1.5 SYNCHRONOUS CONDENSER STARTING SEQUENCE 
The synchronous condenser starting sequence shall be as follows: 
1) A small pony motor (or static frequency converter) shall bring the synchronous condenser up to the network 
synchronous speed with the help of a variable speed drive. 
2) Excitation systems are fully connected, and the voltage and power factor regulators commence operation, 
based on the voltage and power factor reference. 
3) When synchronization is achieved between the network and synchronous condenser, the circuit breaker to 
the power system network is closed.  The synchronous condenser is not running on-line prior to this stage. 
4) After successful synchronization, the pony motor is de-energized and runs ideal with the synchronous 
condenser.

HARMONIC PERFORMANCE 
The SCS shall be designed to avoid elevated harmonic levels at the medium voltage and auxiliary power system 
busses.  The maximum voltage and current distortion generated by the interaction and operation of the SCS equipment 
shall not exceed the recommended value as per IEEE Std. 519 when the SCS is starting or in operation. 
The Contractor shall perform a harmonic performance analysis to identify the resonance conditions expected during 
normal service, over-excitation or under-excitation operation.

It is a requirement of each of the Connection Network Codes (CNCs) that equipment, affected by the 
connection code and connected to the system is compliant with the technical requirements forming 
part of the CNCs at the time that such equipment is first connected and that it then continues to be 
compliant throughout its life. This document describes the Compliance Verification Procedure for 
connection of new Power-Generating Modules (EU regulation 2016/631: NC RfG). The NC RfG has 
been implemented in the Netcode elektriciteit, available in the Dutch language only. All references in 
the English language are unofficial translations of the official Dutch texts in order to be consistent with 
this document.

RfG type definition 
The EU regulation 2016/631 (RfG) defines four types of generators A, B, C and D in Article 5 
“Determination of significance”, as described in chapter 3. The fundamental rationale for creating the 
type definition is that the size of a Power-Generating Module impacts the stability of the grid – the 
larger one single PGM the more impact. The impact of a large amount of small PGM's (e.g. on 
frequency stability) is reflected in the requirements. All requirements in the said regulation are 
cumulative, with some exemptions, sorted into the four types. The compliance testing and simulation 
of Power-Generating Modules follow the same basic principle.

The test will be carried out by simulating frequency steps and frequency ramps at the 
PGM’s control input which are sufficiently large to initiate at least 10% of the Maximum 
Capacity change of the active power, taking into account the droop settings. The frequency 
shall be varied over the full range from 50.0 Hz to 51.5 Hz. After each frequency step or 
ramp the PGM should maintain the new operating point for at least 15 minutes (SPGM) or 2 
minutes (PPM and OPPM) and until the PGM active power output has stabilised. 
As stated in Netcode elektriciteit article: 3.13, sub 4, the LFSM-O activates above a 
frequency threshold of 50.2 Hz. The droop shall be set to 5%. At 5% droop a frequency 
change of 200 mHz above the threshold should cause a change of active power equal to

1. Background 
As a mitigation measure for the reduction of system inertia and short-circuit strength related to the energy 
transition, TenneT is considering the installation of several synchronous condensers, with a machine rating 
between 250 and 400 MVA, at selected 380 kV substations. 
 
Due to the lack of specific internal technical requirements for the connection of synchronous condensers in 
the Netherlands, it is suggested to adopt the following documents as the main basis, and specify relevant 
articles for the definition of the technical requirements which are relevant to synchronous condensers: 
 
i. 
Netherlands implementation of the “RfG requirements for Synchronous Power Generating Modules 
(SPGM) – Type D” [1]. 
ii. 
TenneT GmbH’s “Technical specification of system needs and functions for HVDC and FACTS” [2].

This memo defines what requirements may be applicable for the connection of the synchronous condensers 
for the specific topics of system needs, system functions, testing, simulation and modelling. The rationale is 
that TenneT’s internal requirements should be as strict as the requirements demanded to our customers. 
 
The vendor is responsible for the compliance verification activities, the connection process itself (i.e. how to 
handle the EON, ION and FON phases) is not covered in this document.

2. System needs and functions 
The following list of system needs and functions, based on [2], are relevant for synchronous condensers. 
System needs 
 
Frequency and voltage 
• 
Synchronous condensers and their components shall function, without equipment or performance 
degradation, within the frequency and voltage ranges at the PCC as specified in Section 4.2.7 of [1]. 
• 
Synchronous condensers shall function, without equipment or performance degradation, for 
stepwise changes of the voltage angle between -30° and + 30° at the PCC caused by external 
disturbances. 
 
Power quality 
• 
Synchronous condensers shall fulfil the requirements specified in Section 4.2.20 of [1]. 
• 
Synchronous condensers shall be capable to operate under power quality conditions of Netcode 
Artikel 7.3

The control and protection functions of the synchronous condensers shall avoid any harmful 
interactions with the AC grids which adversely affect either the synchronous condensers protection 
system or the protection systems of the AC grids or other users of the AC grids.

• 
Synchronous condensers shall operate without performance degradation within the whole range 
between minimum and maximum short circuit power at the PCC as specified in a separate 
document: Max. and min. short-circuit levels(CFE380 AMH380 HVL380).xlsx

•

+250 Mvar (overexcited, delivering reactive power) and -125 Mvar (underexcited, absorbing reactive 
power).

The control system of synchronous condensers shall not have a negative influence on the damping 
of power oscillations.

The POD function shall be able to damp power oscillations in the range of 0.1 to 2.0 Hz by active 
modulation of the reactive power exchange at the PCC.

considered in the POD layout.

The Client shall be able to parameterize the POD function via engineering access. The parameters 
will be specified by the Client in the project phase.

It shall be possible for the Client to activate and deactivate the POD function via the HMI.

In summary, the compliance requirements relevant for the synchronous condensers are the following: 
 
Black-start capability (4.2.5) – If applicable 
• 
The synchronous condensers would increase the system strength during the initial phase of the 
black-start restoration procedure and therefore contribute to reducing the risk of over-voltages during 
the energization of large transformers and other electrical equipment.  
• 
This requirement is not required by RfG, but may be required by TenneT.  
• 
To be evaluated via onsite testing at least once per calendar year. 
• 
TenneT may also request to conduct a simulation study to demonstrate the capability. 
 
Frequency range and voltage range (4.2.7) 
• 
To be evaluated via type test reports of the equipment. 
 
Reactive power capability (4.2.8) 
• 
To be evaluated via simulations and onsite testing.

Simulation models 
To perform grid stability studies (RMS) and interaction studies (EMT), the information according Netcode 
elektriciteit article 13.1 and 13.2 shall be delivered, including a full detailed simulation model. Before granting 
the FON (if applicable), the simulation model shall be updated with as-built data and validated with test 
results. 
 
The following requirements apply for the simulation model: 
 
• 
The model shall include all the relevant equipment of the installation up to the Connection Point, i.e. 
flywheel, synchronous condenser, transformers, high-voltage overhead lines or cables, controllers 
and other active components. 
 
• 
The dynamic models of the exciter, power system stabiliser (if applicable) and any other limiters or 
controls shall be described by means of generic terms and parameters given by IEC/IEEE series.

Task 5: PSS®E Power Flow Study
Scope of the Power Flow (i.e. Load Flow) analysis is the evaluation of the steady state
performance of the power plant connected to the national power system.
The analysis is specifically addressed to the assessment of the compliance of the power plant
with the steady state requirements stated in the Grid Code, namely the assessment of the
capability of the SynCon to exchange reactive power with the network over the whole voltage
range as per its capability.
The model of the network in PSS®E supplied by the client shall be used for the calculation.

the SynCon to exchange reactive power with the network over the whole voltage
range as per its capability.
The model of the network in PSS®E supplied by the client shall be used for the calculation. That
shall include all data given, such as loads, generator characteristics, generator dispatching, etc.
The evaluation is made for a limited set of network operating points, maximum of four usually
corresponding to: winter peak load, winter off-peak load, summer peak load, summer off-peak
load. An operating point is a specific state of the power system, defined by the loads (active
and reactive), the dispatching of all power plants and the network conditions, in terms of
components in service.
The network condition is either normal (N), when all the elements are in service, or in
“contingency”, when some elements are out of service.
For network operating point considered, the power flow analysis shall be made in normal (N)
conditions and all N-1 contingency conditions (one transformer or

”, when some elements are out of service.

The objective of this study is to investigate the transient recovery voltage over the 345 kV circuit
breakers of the SynCon while clearing a fault in proximity of the breaker. The calculated TRV is
compared against the capability curves of the circuit breakers provided by the manufacturer,
according to IEC 62271-100. The maximum amplitude and rate-of-rise RRRV are evaluated. It is
not covered by this scope of work the investigation of solutions if needed.
The simulations will be performed with PSCAD™/EMTDC™ v5.0 using standard models of the
involved elements included in the library.

The aim of the harmonic performance study is to examine the expected individual distortions
and the total distortion at the SynCon 345 kV network connection point, secondary supply and
in the SynCon medium voltage auxiliary busbars. The excitation and start-up converters can,
under certain conditions, cause distortions that lead to malfunctions in other equipment. With
this study, such problems can be identified at an early stage and suitable countermeasures can
be initiated.
The results of the investigation are compared with the specified limit values.

This specification provides the Owner’s requirements for the installation of transmission level SCS to provide voltage 
or reactive power control.  The rotating machinery and auxiliary mechanical systems shall be designed for a forty-
year service life.  This specification and appendices, along with supplement specifications as detailed in Section 2 
shall comprise the technical requirements for the engineering, procurement, and installation of a SCS.

cooling systems, protection systems, control systems, step-up power transformer, surge arresters, synchronous 
condenser machine hall, indoor and outdoor switchgear.

condenser machine modules to achieve the required capacity or redundancy.

shall generate an alarm when in operation and when limiter operating points are exceeded.

required, or modifications required, this period shall not be considered part of the trial operation and the SCS shall 
have been deemed to have failed.

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
This document is the Powerlink Queensland Technical Specification and reference document for Synchronous 
Condensers. Together with the Commercial Specification and Project Documents, it will form the Tender 
Specification for Synchronous Condensers and be the technical basis of a supply and install Contract. 
1.2 
Scope 
The scope of works includes the quality assurance, design, manufacture, factory acceptance testing, site 
construction, delivery to site, site installation, site testing, commissioning and energisation (pre and post), 
making good of defects during defects during the Defects Liability Period and selected maintenance as 
service supply of each type of Synchronous Condenser system.

devices. It would also include the measurement of the characteristics of insulating media, washing,

2.14.4 
Failures 
Failures are categorised into: 
a) Critical failure. A failure or combination of failures, which prevent the system from performing the 
whole of the specified duty. 
b) Non-critical failure. A failure, which reduces the reliability of the system but allows continued operation 
for a period of time until servicing can be arranged. Examples of non-critical failures are a failure of 
one of a redundant sub system, and failure of an alarm group.

specification, a non-critical failure is defined as a failure which the failure will reasonably allow further

downtime to rectify. 
2.14.5 
Reliability 
The Reliability of the Synchronous Condenser is the probability of the Synchronous Condenser performing its 
specified duty within a defined time period, where the defined time period must be less than the total time 
period used to determine the Percentage Availability of the Synchronous Condenser.

specified duty within a defined time period, where the defined time period must be less than the total time

Synchronous Condenser can be determined as a percentage, but would be easily confused with the

3. Synchronous Condenser and Components 
3.1 
General Description 
The synchronous condensers shall be capable of continuous unrestricted operation compliance to specified 
requirements in SMM 193 Part 2 Table 2.3.1 with the exception of specified short-term overload requirement 
Since there will be no generation of active power, the synchronous condensers shall be able to continuously 
supply reactive power (capacitive and inductive) up to the practical current limitations.

text:
Since there will be no generation of active power, the synchronous condensers shall be able to continuously 
supply reactive power (capacitive and inductive) up to the practical current limitations. The synchronising 
torque will limit the under-excitation, but for calculations it shall be considered that maximum under-
excitation basically occurs under high voltage grid conditions. 
It is accepted that due to the maximum allowable rotor current the capacitive generation may be restricted 
below the synchronous condenser MVA rating. Likewise, stability concerns (related to the grid) or core-end 
heating problems during under excitation will restrict the inductive absorption. 
The exciter range prescriptions and rating specifications refer to generator/s converted to allow it/ them to 
operate as a synchronous condenser unit/s. For new synchronous condenser units, they shall be designed 
to perform at their specified ratings.

The synchronous condenser shall be installed in the Synchronous Condenser Unit site in a dedicated

3.2 
Stator 
3.2.1 
Stator Core 
The stator core shall be manufactured from low-loss silicon steel ASTM A677 C5 coated punchings held 
under compression by steel end ring (flange) and tooth supports at each end. The core end flanges shall be 
ultrasonically tested and any doubtful area shall be radiographed. Core end shield or other design features 
shall be provided at each core end to limit the core end heating from stray magnetic fields.
source: 10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf
source_path: /mnt/c/Users/z0051yym/Desktop/test_bp_code/knowledge_graph_vector_GC_Data/graph-rag-se-datamodel/data/pdfs/syncon/GC25_122_SynCon_4x_Powerlink/1_Contract_documents/0_RFP/10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf

text:
trasonically tested and any doubtful area shall be radiographed. Core end shield or other design features 
shall be provided at each core end to limit the core end heating from stray magnetic fields. Spring mounted 
core assembly is preferred to limit the transfer of core vibrations to the stator frame.  
Tooth support and duct spacers shall be held securely by a locking mechanism or tack-welding. Segmented 
stator cores shall be securely mounted, at two locations, on dovetail or similarly shaped keys. Filing of slots to 
smoothen out uneven core surfaces is not permitted.  
The core shall be designed to operate within the voltage range 0.95 to 1.07 continuously without exceeding 
the rated temperature rise and with no adverse effect to the core.  
The maximum vibration of the stator core, core frame and windings is preferred to be less than 100 µm peak-
to-peak and no natural resonance shall lie within the frequency ranges 40-65 Hz and 80-130 Hz.

3.8 
Lubrication oil System 
To provide lube oil for the synchronous condenser machine, and pony motor bearings (if required) 
synchronous condenser shall have an independent Lube oil system. 
The lubrication oil system shall be delivered as a fully designed pre-assembled skid. The location of the skid 
shall be away from the synchronous condenser units with a dedicated bunded area with adequate access 
area around the unit. 
The lubrication oil reservoir design shall be such that the NPSH requirement of the oil pumps is met in all 
operating conditions. 
The oil reservoir shall allow for adequate oil dwell time to allow for the separation of entrained air required by 
the lubricating oil specifications

3.9 
Lubrication Oil Pumps 
The lubrication oil system shall have a 100% redundancy in oil pumps to supply lubrication oil to the bearings. 
They shall be fed by AC power supply. An automatic change-over from main to back-up AC pump shall occur 
in case of loss of lubrication oil pressure. 
An emergency DC pump of sufficient capacity shall pump the oil until synchronous condenser comes to a 
complete standstill in case of the grid connection is tripped / lost. The DC pump shall be fed from the 
synchronous condenser units’ dedicated DC battery supply. 
3.10 Jacking Oil System 
A high-pressure jacking oil system shall be incorporated to relieve the friction of the bearings during start-up 
and during the stop process.

3.10 Jacking Oil System 
A high-pressure jacking oil system shall be incorporated to relieve the friction of the bearings during start-up 
and during the stop process. 
The system should include an AC pump, and a back-up DC pump fed from the synchronous condenser unit 
dedicated DC battery supply. 
100% redundancy in inline filters shall be included in the design of the jacking oil system. These shall filter the 
oil down to the necessary particle size and the resultant pressure drop shall be taken into account in the 
design of the system. 
A valve system shall be included to adjust the jacking oil pressure supply to all bearings. The system shall be 
designed so that no oil can flow in the reverse direction through the jacking oil piping while the machine is in 
service. A jacking oil pressure measurement facility shall be provided such that the pressure in the bearing 
(wedge pressure) can be measured at speed.

3.11 Oil Mist Eliminator 
An Oil Mist Eliminator shall be installed to extract the vapour oil from the lubrication oil tank and generate 
vacuum up to the bearings to prevent oil leaks on the shaft seals. 
The Oil Mist Eliminator exhaust shall have an oil vapour separator, ensuring all oil droplets are removed from 
the air stream. The air inlet to the oil tank shall be protected by a suitable air filter. There shall be a 
controllable restriction in the air inlet to be used to alter the under-pressure in the oil reservoir and bearing 
pedestals. 
3.12 Oil Filtration and Heating System 
Inline filtering shall be included in the design of the lubrication system. Two 100% redundant filters shall filter 
the oil down to the necessary particle size.

text:
12 Oil Filtration and Heating System 
Inline filtering shall be included in the design of the lubrication system. Two 100% redundant filters shall filter 
the oil down to the necessary particle size. There shall be alarms for high differential pressure across the 
filters and an emergency filter bypass valve shall be included in the design. 
The pressure drops created by the inline filtration shall be taken into consideration in the design of the 
lubrication system. 
An offline (or “kidney loop”) oil filtration and water removal system shall be provided. 
The system shall include a temperature-controlled heating system that can be used in a bypass mode 
(bypassing the filters) to heat the lubrication oil if required. Protection against accidental overheating of the oil 
shall be provided. 
The offline system inlet and outlet from the oil reservoir shall be designed to ensure adequate oil circulation 
when no oil pumps are in operation.

3.13 Oil/Water Heat Exchanger 
The lubrication oil system shall include oil/water heat exchanger. 
If the water used for cooling of the oil has the potential for heat exchanger fouling, 100% redundancy in oil 
coolers shall be provided, with isolating facilities to allow online cleaning of the water side of the heat 
exchanger. 
An emergency bypass valve shall be included to operate in the case of the oil coolers blocking up on the oil 
side of the heat exchanger.

3.15 Excitation System 
The excitation system for the synchronous condenser shall be brushless. 
The brushless excitation system shall be of well proven design with relevant Inservice references. 
The brushless excitation system shall include all components necessary to apply the appropriate excitation 
voltage to the field of the synchronous condensers for all operating conditions. All equipment necessary to 
fulfil this requirement shall be included. The diodes used shall be suitable for the cyclic loads and forces 
expected from a Synchronous condenser and should be easily accessible for testing and replacement if 
required.

In this control mode, the control system shall regulate reactive power at the connection point or another 
agreed location in the power system. The control system will utilise the Voltage Transformer (VT) and Current 
Transformer (CT) from the high voltage side as provided by the Purchaser. 
The reactive power set point to be continuously controllable across the reactive power capability range of the 
synchronous condenser.  
Synchronous condenser shall has limiting devices to ensure that a voltage at the connection point are always 
in a range of 90% to 110% of the nominal voltage limits or any other defined voltage range. 
The synchronous condenser should not trip at the limits of its operating capability.

binary signals and have open source output files, the preference is for COMTRADE format.

eparate fault recorder shall be installed. It shall have a minimum sampling rate of 8 kHz, be able to capture 
binary signals and have open source output files, the preference is for COMTRADE format. The internal fault 
recorder function of the protection relay shall also be used for recording of the current, the voltage and the trip 
signals during a fault in the electrical system.  
If a trip occurs anywhere within the system, the separate fault recorder shall be triggered by a hardwired

10.4 Reliability centred maintenance 
It is required that Reliability Centred Maintenance (RCM) analysis program shall be carried out straight after 
the energisation of the first Synchronous Condenser System under this Contract. The Purchaser and the 
Contractor shall jointly carry out the RCM analysis program over a period of 2 weeks (10 working days). It is 
envisaged that the preliminary RCM program shall be as follows: 
 
Purchaser’s RCM experts shall discuss the RCM program with the Contractor’s system specialists. 
 
Once the Contractor’s system specialists understand RCM procedures and processes, the 
Purchaser’s RCM experts and the Contractor’s secondary system specialists shall jointly develop a 
comprehensive maintenance program for each Synchronous Condenser System.

11. Maintenance as a Service Supply 
The Contractor shall submit pricing and detailed activity schedule to provide maintenance as a service supply 
for two duration options. 
a) For a twelve (12) year service duration 
b) For a twenty-four (24) year service duration 
The scope of maintenance as a service supply shall cover 
1. Regular Inspections 
 
2. Ordinary Maintenance 
Ordinary Maintenance includes all the maintenance and/or repair activities that do not affect the availability of 
the plant and/or safety on the job and that can be carried out when the component is in operation. Such are 
tasks used for determining specific condition data of the components such as vibrations, temperature, electric 
absorption, etc.

tasks used for determining specific condition data of the components such as vibrations, temperature, electric 
absorption, etc. The lubrication includes activities for verifying the conditions and level of the lubricants on the

Activities include not limited to;

1. Introduction 
1.1 Purpose 
This document is the Technical Specification and reference document for Station Services Transformers and 
Earthing Transformers. Together with the Commercial Specification, it will form the Tender Specification for 
Station Services Transformers and Earthing Transformers and be the technical basis of a supply Contract. 
1.2 Scope 
This specification applies to the quality assurance, design, manufacture, factory acceptance testing, delivery to site, 
and making good of defects during the Defects Liability Period of each type of Station Services Transformer and 
Earthing Transformer for various transmission system requirements.

addition of the following information:



 
Rated continuous current of all windings. 
 
Sealing method. 
 
Mass of core and coils (kg). 
 
Mass of insulating liquid (kg). 
 
Total mass of main transformer in service with oil (kg). 
 
Total oil quantity (l). 
 
Tap changer configuration and vector group.  
 
Transformer Contract Number including Portion Number.

2.3 Current Transformers (CT) and Connections for Earthing Transformers  
All specified current transformers (CT) for earthing transformers shall conform to the requirements of AS 
61869.2 and shall have performance characteristics commensurate with the overload and fault conditions 
defined in ‘Specification Section 6- TABLE 6.1- Summary of Key Technical Requirements’. 
The performance requirements, ratings and diagrammatic location of the CTs on the main transformer windings 
are shown on the relevant Specification Drawings for each item. 
The secondary winding shall be copper. Aluminium is not accepted. The winding connector shall not contain any 
joints. All secondary windings shall have a thermal limit current of not less than 2.0 Per Unit.

Secondary terminals in the CT box shall be marked as per connection diagram as shown on the Rating Plate or 
suitable matching table shall be provided inside or outside the box cover.

distinguishable.

different CT circuits as well as Earth terminals.

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
This Specification covers the design, manufacture, supply, installation, testing, delivery, and rectification of 
defects during the defects liability period of DC Power Systems for Control and Telecommunications 
buildings. 
1.2 
Scope 
The scope of the works includes: 
 
Design of the DC Power System 
 
Manufacture and testing 
 
Delivery to required locations 
 
Installation and commissioning 
 
Rectification of defects during the defects liability period  
 
Removal of existing DC power supply system where applicable 
A strong preference will be given to Suppliers with in-house capabilities including design and manufacture of 
battery cabinets, testing and commissioning services and local en

A strong preference will be given to Suppliers with in-house capabilities including design and manufacture of 
battery cabinets, testing and commissioning services and local engineering support. 
Due to the remote locations of many of sites where the DC Supplies will be installed, reliability and ease of 
maintenance is extremely important. Preference will be given to systems with high MTBF and low MTTR. 
A minimum 15-year design life is required for the battery cells. By design life, this is intended as the time at 
which the battery cells capacity will not fall below 80% at 25ºC. 
A minimum of 20-year design life is required for the battery chargers, and control and monitoring devices.

2. Intended Application 
Powerlink employs integrated DC Power Supplies comprising of battery chargers, batteries, DC distribution, 
and a control / monitoring / alarm system covering both batteries and chargers. The DC Power Supplies 
provide auxiliary DC power for: 
 
Substation control and protection – at 125V DC 
 
Telecommunications systems – at 48V DC. 
Both functions support the operation of the High Voltage Power Transmission network in Queensland. 
The batteries will be on float charge for the majority of their service life with only occasional discharge cycles 
when AC supply is lost to the site or maintenance is carried out. The loss of AC power at High Voltage 
Power Transmission sites is very rare.

Due to the usage of the battery cells in service (generally on float charge with the load being supplied by the 
charger), the Principal places greater emphasis on the service life of the battery cells than on their high-
discharge rate and ability to withstand cycling (frequent charge-discharge). This results in a preference for 
battery cells with a maximum of active material in the cell and thickness of the positive plate.  
DC Power Supplies are required for new installations as well as to replace existing systems in the field which

4. System Requirements 
4.1 
Nominal Output DC Voltages  
The Principal’s substation control and protection systems are powered by nominal 125V DC power supplies.  
The Principal’s telecommunication systems are powered by nominal 48V DC power supplies. 
4.2 
Redundancy of DC Supplies  
The majority of DC systems in substations are Dual DC supplies.  
In 125V DC systems, DC System X and DC System Y are employed. Independent X and Y systems shall be 
designed such that no single point of failure affects both systems.  
In 48V DC systems, DC System A and DC System B are employed. Independent A and B systems shall be 
designed such that no single point of failure affects both systems. 
There are some situations where only a single system is required.

125V DC systems are floating (except for earth detection circuit that may introduce a high impedance 
earthing point).  
In the 125V DC system, a manual make-before-break selector switch is used between the two DC buses. 
This switch is normally in the centre position when X battery/charger supplies X distribution bus and Y 
battery/charger supplies Y distribution bus. If one battery/charger needs to be taken out of service, the switch 
is transferred to the healthy DC side without momentarily losing any bus supply. 
48V DC systems are positive earthed.  
In the 48V DC system, a Bus Tie switch is used. Connection and disconnection of the two buses is manually 
controlled and monitored. The Bus Tie switch is normally open.

4.5 
AC Supply Characteristics 
The DC Power Supplies will be installed at high voltage electricity substations. For various reasons the AC 
supply waveform may not be purely sinusoidal however, harmonics are normally kept within the limits set out 
in AS/NZS 61000.3.6. Most substations are backed up by diesel generators in the event of network AC 
supply failure. Harmonics will appear in the charger AC supply. 
Chargers shall be suitable for connecting to either of the following AC supplies: 
 
Single Phase AC, 230V +10/-11%, 50 HZ +/-2.5%, total harmonic distortion up to 20%.  
 
Three Phase AC, 400/230V +10/-11%, 50 HZ +/-2.5%, total harmonic distortion up to 20%.

The DC Control and Monitoring Systems are to be from the range of the Supplier’s normal production type of

The system shall be capable of both local display and recording of battery charger and battery bank

Figure 4-7- Typical DC Alarm Schematics 
The alarms are normally generated from the Control and Monitoring device, or derived from additional 
external circuitry. The alarms are: 
 
Battery Monitor Alarm – A condition has been detected by the battery monitoring system (mid-point / 
other).  
 
Earth Fault - One of the battery bank poles has developed a condition where its reference to earth 
has changed to above a pre-set value. Both positive and negative pole conditions are to be 
monitored (not applicable for 48V Telecommunications system batteries). 
 
Non Urgent condition – All alarm and fault conditions that occur but have NOT resulted in the 
charging system failing, i.e. the batteries are NOT discharging.
source: 10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf
source_path: /mnt/c/Users/z0051yym/Desktop/test_bp_code/knowledge_graph_vector_GC_Data/graph-rag-se-datamodel/data/pdfs/syncon/GC25_122_SynCon_4x_Powerlink/1_Contract_documents/0_RFP/10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf

text:
lecommunications system batteries). 
 
Non Urgent condition – All alarm and fault conditions that occur but have NOT resulted in the 
charging system failing, i.e. the batteries are NOT discharging. Examples of this condition are: 
communications between the charging module and battery controller have failed, temperature 
sensor has failed, temperature alarm. 
 
Urgent condition – This alarm to be generated ONLY for conditions that result in the batteries 
discharging. Examples of this condition are: AC supply to battery system has failed, all charging 
modules have failed, low battery voltage condition. 
 
Watchdog/Battery controller failure – The battery controller has a fatal problem and has stopped 
functioning to control the charging modules.  
If the Control and Monitoring device is used to generate the alarms, a separate under voltage relay shall be 
connected in parallel with the Urgent Alarm.

nctioning to control the charging modules.  
If the Control and Monitoring device is used to generate the alarms, a separate under voltage relay shall be 
connected in parallel with the Urgent Alarm. This is to ensure the most critical condition of battery 
discharging is monitored in the event of failure of the Control and Monitoring device. The under voltage relay 
is typically set to the same threshold (or slightly lower) as the discharging voltage setting point.

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
This document specifies the required set of SCADA signal and control requirements of Powerlink Queensland to 
fulfil its obligations for the remote control and monitoring of the generation and transmission network connected 
to the National Electricity Market in Queensland.  
The standard approach to operational methodology is promoted by the Network Operations Alarm Management 
Philosophy which is yet to be formalised. 
1.2 
Scope 
The scope of the document is to define the required set of signals from HV substations, power stations, 
communications sites and ancillary equipment to enable the safe and efficient monitoring / operation of the 
infrastructure by Powerlink Queensland to fulfil its obligations.

2. Customers and Providers 
2.1 
SCADA Customers 
2.1.1 
NOS – Network Operations – Control Centre 
The NOC performs the roles of network switching, initial fault management, network analysis and real-time asset 
monitoring. The major tool used to perform these tasks is the EMS which receives the SCADA data. The 
CONTROL CENTRE needs SCADA to carry out the following duties: 
• 
Switching; 
• 
Monitoring transmission system (interconnected and radial) topology of Powerlink Queensland, some 
NSP plant and customer plant connecting to Powerlink Queensland; 
• 
Network/power system real-time condition monitoring of Powerlink Queensland plant; 
•

remotely accessing substation control systems via WAN/Dialup connections.

•

• 
Volts – 0 to +20% nominal value, or +/- 20% of nominal value. 
 
4.4 
Active and Reactive Power Flow Convention 
The following convention is used for active and reactive power flow in Powerlink Queensland substations. This 
convention is applied to transducers and Substation local meters as well as revenue metering equipment. 
The point of reference is chosen as the Substation Bus.   
The bus imports watts from a generator and exports watts to a load.   
The bus imports Vars from a capacitor.

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
The purpose of this document is to define the technical specifications required for provision of Secondary 
Systems Equipment Panels, Marshalling Kiosks and Distribution Boards.  
1.2 
Scope 
This specification covers the design, manufacture, supply, testing and delivery of substation Secondary 
Systems Equipment including Control Panels, Marshalling Kiosks, AC Boards and LV Metering Board. 
Substation Secondary Systems Equipment Panels and associated equipment are used to integrate the primary 
plant with the protection and control systems to provide protection, isolation, control and monitoring.

text:
Secondary Systems Equipment Panels and associated equipment are used to integrate the primary 
plant with the protection and control systems to provide protection, isolation, control and monitoring. The 
Equipment is critical to the operation of the substation and failure of the Equipment will incapacitate the function 
of the substation, which can result in the loss of power.  
 This document refers to ‘Project Design’ which either refers to the detailed design drawings provided by Project 
Design. 
DC Panels (battery chargers, controllers and DC distribution) are not included in this specification. DC panel 
installation in a demountable control building is however included.  
The scope of supply for Secondary Systems Equipment Panels includes but not limited to: 
 
Limited design, where applicable. 
 
Manufacture, including quality assurance. 
 
Assembly and complete wiring.

3. Various Designs and Types 
3.1 
Secondary Systems Equipment Panel Designs and Types 
3.1.1 
General 
Secondary Systems Equipment Panels are normally installed within a demountable Protection and Control 
Building. 
Powerlink uses both swing frame and fixed frame cubicles for Secondary Systems equipment in this 
specification.  
There are three (3) groups of panels: 
 
Primary plant or switching bay related panels - Feeder panels, transformer panels, coupler panels 
and bus zone panels etc. 
 
Common Services related panels - Station panels, Site Infrastructure panels, Network panels, 
Revenue Metering panels, Power Monitoring panels, MUX panels etc.

Secondary Systems Equipment Panel Items

Swing and Fixed Panels 
A typical Protection and Control Panel will have X Protection IEDs mounted in the top of the panel, DC and 
Isolation Link racks located centrally in the panel and the Y Protection and Control IED mounted in the bottom 
portion of the panel, followed by signalling device (if required).

All wiring, unless otherwise specified, shall be carried out in rating of 750V or above annealed copper V90-V90 
PVC insulated wire, installed in accordance with the requirements of AS/NZS 3000. The bulk of this wiring shall 
be in single core multi-strand cable, sized and coloured as shown on the drawings.  
When cables are used in panel wiring instead of single conductor wiring, the exact cable types shown in Project 
Design drawings shall be used. For cable type refer to Project Design drawings.

4.4 
Terminations 
At all times the Contractor shall adhere to the manufacturer’s link or terminal requirements. 
The maximum conductor (or combination of conductor and ferrule) size specified by a link or terminal 
manufacturer shall not be exceeded. Should the design require that a larger wire size be used than what the 
manufacturer specifies for that link or terminal, then direction shall be sought from Project Design before 
proceeding. For push-in terminals care shall be taken not to exceed the manufacturer specification for conductor 
(or combination of conductor and ferrule) size so as not to damage the link or terminal.

ceeding. For push-in terminals care shall be taken not to exceed the manufacturer specification for conductor 
(or combination of conductor and ferrule) size so as not to damage the link or terminal. 
Stranded Conductors (Class 2 – also known as seven strand cable), generally used as field cabling, shall be 
terminated with no crimping lugs for push-in (or tension clamp) links and terminals (with the exception where 
high current AC and DC supply wires are terminated to switch gear (breakers, etc.) where the switch gear 
manufacturer requires a particular type of lug), and Blade lugs for tunnel type (screw-type) links and terminals. 
Flexible Conductors (Class 5 or 6 – also known as multi-strand wiring), generally used within control panels, 
kiosks and boards), shall have insulated bootlace lugs for push-in links and terminals, and Blade lugs for tunnel 
type links and terminals, or lugs to suit the equipment for which the wiring is connecting.

into the control building and the other end in one of the switchyard structures (kiosk, HV plant control box or a 
board). 
Unless specified otherwise on the drawing, field cable screens are earthed at both ends. This requirement 
includes Double Brass tape (DBT) field cables. 
Spare cores in multicore field cables are taped together and earthed at both ends. 
7.5 
Earthing of Panels and Control Building Equipment 
All control and protection Panels, switchboards, battery chargers, termination racks, cableway systems and 
sundry metalwork in all Control Buildings shall be tied to a common earth and bonded via the building Earth to 
the station earthing grid.

continuity, and checked for compliance with the relevant drawings by qualified electrical tradesmen. This testing

1. Purpose 
As a result of PQ Switch Incident 1303 and related ICAM investigations, a new push in CT disconnect terminal 
was investigated to replace the current standard Weidmuller SAKC10 due to safety concerns presented with 
screw type terminals becoming loose and releasing the wire resulting in an open circuit CT secondary. 
This Standards Update recommends a new CT push in disconnect terminal, Phoenix P/P HV OG, to be installed 
on all CT circuits for all current and future projects. 
This Standards Update has been produced in lieu of circuitry template updates which will occur under project 
OR.2237.

4. Detail 
The Phoenix PT6-T P/P HV OG (Phoenix part number 1068179) push in physical disconnect terminal shall 
replace the current standard Weidmuller SAKC10 screw type physical disconnect terminal for all CT circuits in 
Protection and Control Panels, Termination Racks and Marshalling Kiosks.   
The colour of this terminal has been selected to be orange – i.e. orange body and black plug – so that CT 
terminals remain easily distinguishable. 
 
 
Figure 1 – PT6-T P/P HV OG Physical Disconnect Terminal.

text:
of this terminal has been selected to be orange – i.e. orange body and black plug – so that CT 
terminals remain easily distinguishable. 
 
 
Figure 1 – PT6-T P/P HV OG Physical Disconnect Terminal. 
 
The PT6 terminal is physically narrower (10mm width) than the SAKC10 (12mm width) so it will not consume 
any additional DIN rail space with physical dimensions 10mm width x 91mm length x 64.3mm height.   
The PT6 terminal is fully encased so there is no requirement for end plates.   
Spacer plates, DP-PT 6-T P/P HV-1,8 (Phoenix part number 1028592), will be used to provide delineation 
between different CT circuits as well as Earth terminals. 
Adjacent terminals may be bridged on either side of the PT6 terminal via a plug-in bridge – Phoenix accessory 
FBS 5-10 (Phoenix part number 3005948) – which can be cut to length to suit bridging requirements.

5. Bay Packages 
The new PT-6 terminal shall be installed on all CT circuits for bay packages in Protection and Control Panels, 
Termination Racks and Marshalling Kiosks. 
The PT-6 terminal configuration limits multiple wire terminations at an individual termination point (unlike the 
SAKC10 screw type terminal where two wire terminations are permitted).  Additional terminals will need to be 
installed in the Bay Marshalling Kiosk to accommodate the bridging in going from a 6-wire CT system (A-N, B-N, 
C-N) to a 4-wire CT system (A-B-C-N).  Adjacent terminals may be bridged on either side of the terminal via 
plug-in bridges.

6. Bus Zone Package 
The new PT-6 terminal shall be installed on all CT circuits for bus zone packages in Protection and Control 
Panels, Termination Racks and Marshalling Kiosks. 
CTs from bays connected to a single bus are summated in the Bus Zone Marshalling Kiosk.  The HZBZ 
template caters for up to 15 connected bays per bus – thus requiring bridging of up to 15 CT circuits per phase. 
In order to accommodate this bridging, PTFIX 18X2,5-NS35 OG (Phoenix part number 3273194) Distribution 
Blocks will be used (in colour OG – orange).  These blocks provide bridging for up to 18 inputs.   
The dimensions of the PTFIX Distribution Block are 46.9mm width x 45.7mm length x 30.9mm height.

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
The purpose of this document is to detail Powerlink’s technical requirements for multicore cables. These 
technical requirements shall be read in conjunction with other contract documents. 
1.2 
Scope 
The multicore cables specified in this document will be used for Control signals or Power circuits. The multicore 
cables are used in high voltage electrical substations, installed either outdoor or within buildings. 
Two basic types of multicore cables are specified in this document.

2.3 
Core Joints 
Joints shall not be permitted in conductors of any size. Any cables found to have joints will be rejected and the 
supplier will be required to replace the relevant cable at its own cost. 
2.4 
Metallic Screen/Insect Resistant Barrier 
A metallic electrostatic screen shall be incorporated into the cable to collectively screen all cores. The screen 
shall consist of a double brass tape with extruded bedding applied in accordance with AS/NZS 5000.1 and 
AS/NZS 5000.3. 
The double brass tape metallic screen shall also serve as an insect barrier. 
The double brass tape metallic screen shall have a fault current carrying capacity not less than the equivalent of 
2.5 sqmm PVC V90 copper wire under the same installation conditions.

3. Testing 
The cable shall be tested in accordance with the requirements of the applicable AS/NZS Standards and a copy 
of all test certificates detailing the results of all tests carried out by the Supplier shall be submitted upon delivery 
of the cable. 
Type test certificates shall be submitted either at the time of tendering or at the time of the first delivery of cable. 
Routine and special test certificates shall be submitted at the time of each delivery. 
Test certificates shall clearly show the purchaser’s order number, the cable type and quantity. 
All test certificates shall be in PDF format.

4. Packaging 
4.1 
Drum Requirements 
4.1.1 
Construction 
All cable shall be supplied on wooden drums in accordance with AS/NZS 2857. Timber for drums shall be 
industrial grade material, sound and free from defects that could materially weaken or adversely affect the 
component parts of the drum or have a detrimental effect on the cable. Suppliers shall provide details of the 
type of timber to be used, moisture content and preservative treatment. 
Fittings e.g. barrel bolts, are to be secured in such a manner to remain tight for the duration of transport and 
storage, in accordance with AS/NZS 2857. 
All nuts and bolts are to comply with the relevant requirements of AS 1111 and AS 1112.

4.1.2 
Flanges and Booker Rods 
 
Flanges shall be constructed from three layers of timber, with the outer layer of the flange to be a 
minimum size width of 150mm.  
 
Each flange layer must be adequately secured together, and appropriately nailed throughout the flange 
board to ensure that the structural stability of the flange will meet storage requirements set out within. 
 
A minimum of five booker rods should be used, and more for larger capacity drums (Supplier to indicate 
at tender time the adequate number of booker rods for their products for certain size drums). 
 
Booker rod is to be secured on both sides of the flange, with a spring washer and nut.

The cable shall be protected by external lagging to ensure that it is delivered undamaged giving due

Nailing of the lagging must be nailed through timber, not between the flange layers.

Durability 
Cable drums supplied are to be suitable to withstand a minimum of 24 months outdoor storage in all types of 
weather conditions without deterioration. 
4.2 
Cable Length and Winding 
Drums shall contain continuous cable lengths of 200m, 300m, 500m or 1000m as specified. A cutting tolerance 
of -5% or + 10% may be accepted by the Purchaser providing a request for acceptance is issued to the 
Purchaser immediately upon manufacture. The cable shall be in one continuous length on each drum. No joints 
shall be permitted.

conjunction with the other applicable conditions of contract / contract documents.

1.1 
Purpose 
The purpose of this specification is to ensure that all equipment that connects to Powerlink’s OT (Operational 
Technology) network, adheres to Powerlink’s Cyber Security and Information Security requirements. This will 
assist with Powerlink’s ability to meet the requirements of QLD Government Information Security Policy 
IS18:2018, and the Australian Energy Sector Cyber Security Framework (AESCSF) and/or its successors. 
This specification is intended for release as part of Powerlink ROI (Registration of Interest) and ITT (Invitation to 
Tender) documentation.

1. Introduction
1.1 
Purpose 
This document is the Technical Specification and reference document for Large Power Transformers. Together 
with the Commercial Specification, it will form the Tender Specification for Large Power Transformers and be 
the technical basis of a supply and install Contract. 
1.2 
Scope 
This specification applies to the quality assurance, design, manufacture, factory acceptance testing, delivery to 
site, site installation, site pre-commissioning testing and making good of defects during the Defects Liability 
Period of each type of power transformer for various transmission system requirements. 
2.

2. Design and Construction
2.1 
Ratings 
The transformers shall be rated for continuous operation at any tapping position at the specified ratings without 
exceeding the temperature rise limits set out in Clause 9, Summary of Key Technical Requirements. 
 
 
2.3 
Emergency Overload Capacity 
Under emergency conditions, the transformer to be overloaded for extended periods on any tapping within the 
constraints that the winding hot-spot temperature would be limited to 140 deg. C and / or top oil temperature 
limited to 115 deg. C, with the winding hot-spot temperature calculated as set out in AS66076 or measured by 
fibre-optic temperature probes imbedded in the windings.

limited to 115 deg. C, with the winding hot-spot temperature calculated as set out in AS66076 or measured by 
fibre-optic temperature probes imbedded in the windings. 
It is envisaged that, dependent on ambient conditions on site, this emergency overload condition may reach the 
MVA value specified in Clause 9, Summary of Key Technical Requirements. To meet this requirement, all 
internal leads, High Voltage (HV) and Low voltage (LV) bushings and connections to HV and LV bushings, and 
Current Transformers (CT) shall all have minimum current ratings that equal this overload current rating. On 
Load Tap Changer (OLTC) ratings, refer Clause 9, Summary of Key Technical Requirements. 
The design shall be such that local overheating due to stray losses does not occur for rated and emergency 
overload conditions. Localised temperature rise in tank fittings and internal components other than windings, in 
excess of 75 deg. C at rated load and 15 deg.

2.4 
Operation Conditions 
2.4.1 
Impedance and Parallel Operation 
Transformer shall be suitable for operating in parallel with other transformers in service. The impedance and 
ratio characteristics required are listed in Clause 9, Summary of Key Technical Requirements. 
HV/ LV impedances shall match within a tolerance of ± 5% of specified value at all tap positions. Exact tapping 
ratios shall be approved prior to commence manufacturing, if they deviate from those specified in Clause 9, 
Summary of Key Technical Requirements by more than 0.1%.

2.4.2 
Geomagnetically Induced Current 
When a particular design is subjected to Geomagentically Induced Currents (GIC) and applicable GIC current 
and duration is specified in Clause 9; Summary of Key Technical Requirements, the design shall be capable to 
handle  
•
Increased magnetic flux density in core and magnetising current
•
Increased vibration and noise
•
Increased temperature rise in transformer windings and structural parts due to additional stray flux
•
Harmonics in current
•
Increased reactive power absorption
2.5 
Audible sound level and vibration 
Designed average sound power shall not exceed the levels specified in Clause 9, Summary of Key Technical 
Requirements.

2.5 
Audible sound level and vibration 
Designed average sound power shall not exceed the levels specified in Clause 9, Summary of Key Technical 
Requirements. 
At the substation, transformer shall be placed on a flat concrete base with anti-vibration pads of at least 30 mm 
thickness and made from oil resistant synthetic rubber. The anti-vibration pads shall be arranged to achieve 
even and optimum compression and vibration damping in service. Shall provide evidence of calculations made 
to achieve optimum vibration damping. 
Hot dipped galvanised or stainless-steel shim plates shall also be supplied as required to provide on even load 
distribution from the transformer main tank base to the anti-vibration pads.

Hot dipped galvanised or stainless-steel shim plates shall also be supplied as required to provide on even load 
distribution from the transformer main tank base to the anti-vibration pads.  
The design of the main magnetic circuit (including flux shunts), main tank and their individual members shall 
fulfil the requirement of natural frequencies of vibration shall not coincide with, or approximate to, the frequency 
of the magnetic forces or their harmonics. 
2.6 
Current transformers 
All specified Current Transformers (CT) shall conform to the requirements of AS 61869.

2.8.7

2.8.7.1 
Construction of Windings 
The design shall promote the elimination of partial discharges within the transformer at the test voltages. 
“Electro-Static analysis” of the complete insulation structure based on Finite Element Modelling shall be carried 
out and the field plots shall be provided as part of the Design Review documentation. Safety margin between 
the corona inception field strength and the calculated corona inception field stress values shall have a minimum 
20% safety margin for degassed oil. The corona inception field strength shall be referenced to the published 
Kepller curves (in Weidmann book Band 1, Volume1).

to prevent dislocation under transport and normal and abnormal operating conditions including short circuit

mechanical bracing back to the central core.

Tertiary Winding Design 
The product of the number of turns per phase of the tertiary winding and the cross-sectional area of one such

25% of the corresponding product for the main winding equivalent [(series + common turns) x copper

•

Tap position.

Current splitting tapping winding designs shall not be used.

2.8.7.4 
Short Circuit Withstand 
The windings shall be adequately braced against mechanical and electrical vibration and stresses and capable 
of withstanding the effect of an external short circuit in accordance with AS/NZS 60076.5.  
Three phase symmetrical system fault levels for short circuit withstand design are provided in Clause 9, 
Summary of Key Technical Requirements. 
Pre-fault operating voltage of Um and ‘K’ asymmetry factor of 1.9 shall be applied for short circuit withstand 
capability calculations. 
A single piece top clamping ring with uniform thickness shall be provided.

2.8.7.6 
Magnetic Circuit – Core 
The magnetic circuit shall be insulated from core bolts and supporting framework. A separate insulated 
removable bolted earth link shall be provided for earthing of the core and another for earthing of the core 
support framework. These links shall be protected in a metal box located externally on the transformer and 
arranged so they are accessible for testing purposes without having to open up the transformer. The metal box 
shall be fitted with an oil tight cover to seal against bushing oil leaks and a stainless-steel engraved label to 
identify the location of these earth links shall be mounted on the metal box cover.

2.8.7.7 
Flux Density 
A prime concern is sound level and core saturation effects in the transformer, especially under conditions of 
high input voltages. It is therefore required that the highest flux density within the core shall not exceed figure 
specified in Clause 9, Summary of Key Technical Requirements for any tapping position and for any winding / 
tap changer configuration. 
“Electro-Magnetic Analysis” of the design based on Finite Element Modelling of surface of core, core frames, 
core clamps, tie rods, tank base, tank wall, tank cover, bushing turrets, disconnection chambers and leakage 
flux control devices shall be carried out for maximum name plate rating and emergency overload rating. Flux 
plots, calculated flux density values, calculated loss densities and calculated temperature rise values shall be 
provided as part of the Design Review documentation.

Active Parts Final Clamping 
Final winding compression (clamp down) shall be by three (3) phase simultaneous clamping. 
Shall provide full details on number/type of jacks, applied pressure, special equipment details/drawings, 
instructions and how to re-clamp the coils. 
Shall also provide methods for verifying the residual winding clamping pressure after the final clamp down has 
been completed. 
This information shall be also included in the transformer “For Construction” and “As Built” Manual including 
colour photos taken during the clampdown.

2.8.9 
Vacuum and Pressure 
The tank, the conservator, coolers, and associated pipe work shall be capable of withstanding without permanent 
deformation: 
•
Full vacuum.
•
An internal pressure of 50 kPa in excess of the pressure required to operate the pressure relief valve,
when measured at the pressure relief valve, with the transformer full to its normal in-service level.
The pressure relief valve shall be able to close against the head of oil pressure when the conservator is full of 
oil.

2.8.13 
Safety Harness Attachment Rings and Safety Rail System 
2.8.13.1 
Safety Harness Attachment Rings 
Safety harness attachment rings rated to 21 kN load, or greater, for a ‘Restrained Fall’ for two (2) people shall 
be provided for safe working on the top of the transformer, cooler bank and around the conservator.  
Approved safety harness attachment ring is Rud lashing point type VRS-F-M20 as per Specification drawing H-
121457-003. 
Safety harness attachment rings shall be placed in consideration of climbers/workers using lanyards of 1 metre 
maximum length i.e. first attachment point reachable from the top of the ladder, each successive anchor 
reachable from every other attachment point as they move about on the top of the transformer.

2.8.15 
Lifting and Jacking Arrangements 
Facilities shall be provided to permit lifting all parts that may have to be removed for inspection or repair. Lifting 
lugs shall be provided to lift the unit as a whole and to secure it to a transporter. Jacking lugs shall be provided 
near each corner of the transformer at a height of at least 350 mm above ground level with the transformer 
resting on the foundations. These lugs shall have holes for haulage and slewing. Alternatively, separate lugs 
shall be provided for this purpose. 
Provision shall be made that jacking from one jacking point shall not cause permanent damage to active parts 
and deformation of the tank.  
Each component that may be removed from the transformer tank shall be supplied with lifting lugs.

arresters as specified in Clause 9, Summary of Key Technical Requirements and the specified wind loading and 
fault rating forces. The mounting brackets shall be hot dip galvanized to AS 4680 after fabrication.  
Shall provide removable surge arrester mounting brackets for the HV, LV and TV (when fully brought out in 
three phase transformers) adjacent to the phase bushings of the transformer.  
HV and LV surge arresters are supplied and installed by others. Refer to Surge Arrester drawings provided for 
each transformer.

2.8.17 
Main Pipework 
The main oil pipework connecting the main tank to the cooler bank shall be designed to eliminate oil flow 
turbulence and provide laminar oil flow for oil directed designs, especially in the location of the oil flow switch 
transducer mounting. 
Non-Return Valves for oil directed designs shall not hammer excessively when an oil pump starts and shall be 
installed only in horizontal pipe sections. Non-Return Valves shall not be installed on an angle.  
The starting of the oil pump(s) shall not cause a significant, mechanical impulse through the pipework and 
connecting structures.

The transformer shall be fitted with an oil conservator incorporating the following features: 
(a) The conservator shall be of a horizontal cylindrical shape. The main conservator tank shall be provided 
with a fully partitioned chamber, with the same diameter as the main tank conservator, for the tap 
changer conservator. 
(b) An air cell of approved make shall be installed and shall fully seal the transformer oil system from direct 
contact with the external atmosphere. Only bags from manufacturers with a proven track record of 
supply of bags that have performed satisfactory in service for more than 15 years will be considered.  
(c) An air cell rupture monitoring device shall be mounted on the top at the highest point of the conservator 
tank to indicate if the air cell becomes ruptured and / or develops a leak allowing free gas to enter the 
conservator volume normally occupied only by oil.

2.8.24 
Oil Joints and O-Rings 
All joints on the transformer shall be rendered completely oil tight. Past experience has proven that even the 
smallest oil weeps develop into oil leaks under service conditions. 
Metal surfaces of oil joints on all flanges shall be machined, grooved, and fitted, where physically possible, with 
double O-rings or other type of seals with proven “in service performance”. . 
Where flat gasket type seals are used, Nitrile or higher grade rubber gasket shall be used. Cork types of 
gaskets shall not be used. 
Screwed joints shall not be used where oil tightness is required.

2.8.27.1 
Cooling Equipment 
Each transformer Item shall have the cooling classification listed in Clause 9, Summary of Key Technical 
Requirements  
The radiators shall be of a robust, compact, maintenance free design and construction and shall be fabricated of 
hot dip galvanised steel. The radiators shall be demountable with machined flanges and shall require approval. 
When specified as directed oil cooling, the transformer shall be provided with two oil circulating pumps of a 
glandless oil immersed type, with each pump rated to provide the cooling capacity required for the full OD 
transformer rating with one pump out of service. This design shall be approved.

3. Painting and Corrosion Prevention  
3.1 
General 
3.1.1 
Scope 
The intent of this part is to ensure that all surfaces of transformers and associated equipment, other than those 
specifically excluded, shall be finished with an appropriate coating system that will provide the necessary 
protection against corrosion, with minimal maintenance, for the design life of the structures and equipment. 
All equipment and materials, requiring such protection, unless specifically excluded, shall receive coating 
systems as specified herein, or an approved alternative coating systems.  
A standard paint and corrosion protection system could be offered, as an alternative provided it gives equal or 
better corrosion protection than the system specified herein. .

All surfaces of structures and equipment, other than those specifically excluded, shall be finished with an 
appropriate coating system that will provide the necessary protection against corrosion, with minimal 
maintenance, for the design life of the structures and equipment. 
The excluded surfaces are: 
(a) Plated metals or metals specifically finished for appearance including bronze, brass, copper, and 
stainless steel (except when required for piping identification). 
(b) Aluminium (except where specifically required for appearance). 
(c) Inside of structural elements totally sealed by welding.

Specification.

General 
Surface preparation and the application of surface coatings are special processes as referred to in Process 
Control of AS/NZS ISO 9000.2. Shall submit documentation giving full details of the special process procedures 
for each surface preparation/coating application system.

of AS 1580. 
3.3.3

AS3894.

3.3.4 
Coatings Dry Film Thickness Acceptance Criteria 
The minimum dry film thickness of each coating shall be as specified in Clause 3.5.3. Coatings shall be defined 
as the "minimum dry film thickness (DFT" for use in the following acceptance criteria. 
"The measurement of dry film thickness (DFT) shall be made in accordance with AS 3894.3 and the Inspection 
Objectives of that Standard Method shall be adopted as the acceptance criteria for coatings applied under this 
Specification". In the event that the specified minimum thickness is not achieved, additional coats shall be 
applied until the required thickness is obtained. Inorganic zinc coatings shall not be corrected in this manner.

3.3.5 
Workmanship 
Preparation of the substrate and application of the coatings shall be in accordance with ISO 12944-7 Paints and 
varnishes — Corrosion protection of steel structures by protective paint systems — Part 7: Execution and 
supervision of paintwork. 
The minimum dry film thickness of each coating shall be as specified in Clause 3.5.3. Coatings shall be defined 
as the "minimum DFT" for use in the acceptance criteria required under ISO 12944-7 Section 5 General. 
3.3.6 
Repair to Damaged Coatings 
All damaged, or burnt and degraded coatings shall be completely removed, exposing a clean substrate or a 
coating free of imperfections.

3.3.6 
Repair to Damaged Coatings 
All damaged, or burnt and degraded coatings shall be completely removed, exposing a clean substrate or a 
coating free of imperfections. All edges of damaged coatings shall be feathered back as necessary to achieve a 
smooth uninterrupted surface. The method used to clean such areas shall be power tool cleaning in accordance 
with AS1627, Part 2, or ISO 8504-3, with the exception of corrosive areas that shall be abrasive blast cleaned in 
accordance with AS1627, Part 4 or ISO 8504-2. 
The patches of new paint should overlap the old paint by at least 50 mm except for inorganic zinc coatings and 
etch primers that must not overlap existing top coats. 
Damage shall be repaired by recoating affected areas in the same or equivalent manner to that originally 
specified in this Specification under Clause 3.5, Coating and Protective Systems.

3.5.2 
Temporary Protective Systems 
These systems are intended to protect prepared surfaces during transport and storage. They are temporary in 
that they are required to be removed prior to placing the particular equipment in operation, or will be removed by 
normal operation of the equipment. 
All temporary protective systems shall conform in general to BS 1133 Packaging Code - and in particular to 
Section 19, "Use of Desiccants in Packaging". 
(a) Temporary Protective 1 
(i) Apply a coating of oil over the entire surface. The oil shall be that which will be used during the 
service life of the equipment. 
(ii) Include a suitable desiccant, according to BS 1133: Section 19 sufficient to remove all moisture 
from the enclosed space for the entire storage period. 
(iii) Seal moisture-tight.

3.6 
Preparation and coating schedule 
The following schedule summarises the surface preparation and the protective coating systems required and 
detailed in this Specification for the main elements, but it does not necessarily include all components to be 
supplied. 
Note 1: All coatings used shall be entirely suitable for use on oil filled transformers and shall not 
deteriorate when in contact with transformer insulating oils.  
Note 2: Cleaned condition shall mean free of all extraneous matter and scale and shall be of bright 
white metal appearance without discolouration due to oxidation. Details of the method proposed to 
obtain this 'cleaned' condition shall be submitted. 
Note 3:"Proprietary Equipment" is defined as that equipment which is not specifically manufactured.

3.7 
Paint repair on site after transportation and installation 
3.7.1 
Scope 
This specification details the requirements for repairs to existing coatings as nominated by markings, drawings 
or otherwise directed. Nominated surfaces of structures and equipment, other than those specifically excluded, 
shall be repaired with an appropriate coating system which will provide the necessary protection against 
corrosion, with minimal maintenance, for the design life of the existing coating system or the structures and 
equipment whichever the lesser.  
Coatings shall be reinstated using a system directly equivalent to the existing system unless departures are 
specifically allowed.

Toxic Substrate 
Items containing toxic elements in the substrate (lead, chromate, asbestos) as listed in Table 3-3 shall be

Topcoat damaged, primer intact 
High pressure water blasting may be used to remove poorly adhering topcoat if not restricted under Table 3-.3. 
Topcoats, and where present intermediate coats, shall be sanded back to give a smooth and fair, strongly-

the coating to be applied.  
Where damage to coatings is especially numerous and/or extensive and Table 3-3 restrictions permit, abrasive 
blast cleaning may be employed.

4.1 
AC and DC Supplies to Transformer Auxiliary Equipment  
All AC and DC power supplies required for the operation of the transformer auxiliary equipment will be provided 
in the form of one general purpose 400/230 VAC 3 phase and Neutral 50 Hz 4 wire supply, 125 VDC supply to 
the Main Control Cubicle and 24 VDC supply for oil and winding temperature transducers. Shall provide all 
distribution beyond those points. 
4.2

For a free standing cooler bank, shall provide a Main Control Cubicle positioned on the cooler bank or on a free 
standing hot dipped galvanised stand and a separate CT Marshalling / Metrosil Cubicle mounted on the main 
transformer tank.
