Pressure Tests on Tank and Coolers. 
Pressure tests shall be carried out on the transformer assembled complete with conservator, 
radiators and other fittings (pressure relief valves clamped). These tests shall be carried out with 
the transformer filled with insulating oil and the air cell installed and correctly inflated. The oil head 
shall be measured from the highest point on the main tank conservator. The pressure shall be 
equalized between the OLTC diverter tank barrier, the main tank, and the air cell.  
The test is required to prove that: 
(i) The tank has sufficient mechanical strength to withstand the pressure required to operate 
the pressure relief valve with a safety margin of 50 kPa. 
The pressure applied shall be "the pressure required to operate the pressure relief valve + 
50 kPa". It shall be deemed that the plant has passed if tank deflection is < 5 mm, when 
the pressure is released, after being held at the level required for 10 minutes.

(ii) The transformer, radiators, conservator and all the fittings are oil tight and free from leaks.

text:
Relay Stability Test. 
To test that the Buchholz Relay does not operate inadvertently during pump starts, cold and hot oil 
pump starts shall be performed on all transformers equipped with oil pumps. All valves between the 
transformer tank and the conservator shall be open and the air cell vented freely to the atmosphere 
via the desiccant breather. The tests shall be performed with the Buchholz relay set or calibrated to 
trip at a flow rate not exceeding 100 cm/sec and otherwise as follows 
(i) Cold oil Buchholz relay stability test - this test shall be performed with the top oil 
temperature at 20 – 30 deg. C and a voltage of 110% of normal 400 V AC applied to the 
motor terminals, and... Ten (10) pump starts shall be carried out on each possible 
combination of pumps selected for duty/standby with oil flow ceasing between each start. 
The transformer is deemed to have passed the test if neither the Buchholz relay trip or 
alarm contacts closes during any of the tens starts.

6.1 
Packing 
All ancillary equipment shall be crated and packed suitable for outdoor storage without deterioration or damage 
to its contents. 
Crates and packing shall be of a robust construction and shall be capable of withstanding without damage, 
transport over rough roads for long distances, and long term storage outdoors up to twelve (12) months. 
Crates shall be suitable for being lifted by crane.  
All connection flanges shall be fitted with substantial covers to prevent damage to the flange and its mating 
surfaces and to prevent ingress of moisture.

6.4 
Transport conditions 
6.4.1 
Road Transport 
Limitations on transport height and axle load apply for heavy lifts on Australian public roads and certain sections 
of the transport route may require detours from the main Highway. Shall carry out reconnaissance of the whole 
of the route to ensure that the mode of transport and the route selected is feasible.  
6.4.2 
Transport of Transformer Tank and Oil to Site 
The transformer tank shall be transported to site with oil drained off for transport.

text:
the mode of transport and the route selected is feasible.  
6.4.2 
Transport of Transformer Tank and Oil to Site 
The transformer tank shall be transported to site with oil drained off for transport. The transformer tank and the 
radiators shall be filled and remain filled with dry air during transport and whilst awaiting erection on site. The 
main tank for the transformer shall be equipped with a regulated backup supply of dry air which shall maintain a 
small, above atmosphere positive pressure of 10 - 20 kPa gauge during transport to site and whilst the 
transformer is awaiting erection. Dry air shall have a dew point better than - 40 deg. C. 
Dry Nitrogen shall not be used during transport and whilst awaiting erection on site. 
The pressurising system shall be supplied with sufficient dry air to maintain the above pressure on the 
transformer tank for at least six (6) months. The initial quantity of dry air supplied shall not be less than of two 
type ‘G’ cylinders.

ith sufficient dry air to maintain the above pressure on the

type ‘G’ cylinders. 
The dry air pressurising the system shall have a safety-venting valve fitted to prevent over pressurising of the 
tank. 
• 
In the event of a transformer arriving on site with the tank pressure equal to or less than atmospheric 
pressure, the high voltage insulation dryness shall be determined by the transformer manufacturer. The 
transformer high voltage winding insulation shall be subjected to a dielectric loss angle measurement at 
10 kV rms and if the measured tangent delta is equal to or greater than 0.005 or the insulation moisture 
content exceeds 1.0% by Dielectric Response Analysis (IDAX/DIRANA), the transformer insulation shall 
be dried.

6.4.3 
Impact Recording 
Shall provide and fit an impact-recording device to the transformer at the factory prior to loading it onto the 
transporter for transport to the delivery site. The recorder shall be able to record and time stamp any impact 
above 0.5 G occurring in any of the three dimensions during the whole of the transport journey, up until it is 
resting in its final position on the designated plinth. 
The recordings from the impact recorder shall be recovered immediately after the transformer has been 
positioned on its plinth and a copy of the recordings shall be provided. Where special software is required to 
interpret the recorded data held by the impact recorder, they shall supply an interpreted copy of the recordings.

Multicore Cable Terminations 
(a) The outer sheath of the multicore cable shall be removed immediately beyond the terminating 
gland, cable clamp or cable tie-off point. The metallic earthing screen shall be removed down 
to a projecting band and connected to earth or insulated in accordance with the construction 
drawing. Where earthing is required, the drain wire used for earthing shall be a minimum 2.5 
mm2 stranded green yellow tinned copper wire. 
(b) The cores of each individual multicore cable shall be kept together as far as possible until the 
cores need to be separated to enter the terminals. 
(c) Where required, each end of a core shall be provided with lettered ferrules to identify the core 
number as shown on the construction drawings (namely the schematic diagram and 
connection schedules).

text:
here required, each end of a core shall be provided with lettered ferrules to identify the core 
number as shown on the construction drawings (namely the schematic diagram and 
connection schedules). 
(d) Where possible, the cores shall be run into the terminals horizontally such that any 
identification ferrules are immediately visible and clearly readable 
(e) Ferrules shall:  
• 
be made of insulating materials;  
• 
be fitted firmly on the insulation of the wire as close as possible to the terminal;  
• 
have black letters on white background;  
• 
be read from left to right when installed in the horizontal plane; and  
• 
be read bottom to top when installed in the vertical plane.  
(f) The weight of the multicore cable shall be taken by the cable gland, cable clamp or cable ties 
and no pressure or tension shall be exerted on the terminal.  
(g) All cores, including spare cores, shall be terminated on terminals provided.

and no pressure or tension shall be exerted on the terminal.  
(g) All cores, including spare cores, shall be terminated on terminals provided.  
(h) Spare cores shall:  
• 
be left equal to the longest terminated core in the cable and shall be laid back and 
neatly secured to the parent cable where there are no terminals for spare cores;  
• 
be connected together and connected to earth, whether terminated or laid back, 
unless nominated otherwise on the connection schedules; and  
• 
be left with a 2.5 m tail for the termination work at the protection and control panels 
(i) The construction drawings (namely the schematic wiring diagram) shall be used for 
connection and numbering purposes of cable cores. 
(j) The Contractor shall comply with the terminal manufacturer requirements for termination,

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
The purpose of this Specification is to provide the technical requirements for a greenfield Synchronous 
Condenser installation. 
1.2 
Scope 
This document specifies the requirements for civil works, buildings, structural steelwork and foundations 
associated with the design and construction of a Synchronous Condenser. 
2. Civil Works, Buildings, Structural Steelwork and Foundations 
The Contractor shall be responsible for the design, supply and construction of all civil work, structural steelwork, 
buildings, foundations and earthworks necessary for the establishment of the Synchronous Condensers, 
including but not limited to: 
 
Geotechnical investigation for the substation area for design purposes.

 
The foundations shall cater for both static loads plus dynamic and vibrational (frequency and amplitude) 
forces. 
 
The concrete grade shall not be less than 32MPa.  
 
N500 reinforcing shall be used in concrete foundations 
 
In mass concrete, hydration temperature gradients result in a difference between the core and zones 
near the surface and the concrete bottom. This shall be effectively controlled and monitored to be well 
below 200 C during concrete curing. This is required to limit internal thermal stresses and prevent 
significant thermal cracking where the concrete tensile strength has not fully developed at the early 
stages of hydration. Evidence of control measures adopted shall be provided to the Principal for 
acceptance.
source: 10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf
source_path: /mnt/c/Users/z0051yym/Desktop/test_bp_code/knowledge_graph_vector_GC_Data/graph-rag-se-datamodel/data/pdfs/syncon/GC25_122_SynCon_4x_Powerlink/1_Contract_documents/0_RFP/10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf

text:
hermal cracking where the concrete tensile strength has not fully developed at the early 
stages of hydration. Evidence of control measures adopted shall be provided to the Principal for 
acceptance.  
 
A dynamic analysis shall be conducted to assess vibration transmission paths and optimise damping 
solutions to mitigate structural and operational impacts. 
 
An expansion gap shall be provided around the machine foundation and the building floor slab and filled 
with suitable insulating materials to effectively isolate foundation vibrations being transmitted to 
surrounding plant and structures. 
 
Where machine foundations are embedded in rock, a vibration isolation perimeter around the rock mass 
shall be provided to prevent vibration transmission.  
 
The foundation shall have adequate mass to absorb vibrations and prevent resonance. The mass of the 
foundation block should be approximately 3 (or more) times that of the machine.

text:
transmission.  
 
The foundation shall have adequate mass to absorb vibrations and prevent resonance. The mass of the 
foundation block should be approximately 3 (or more) times that of the machine. 
 
The natural frequency of the machine-foundation-soil system shall not be within the range of -10hz to 
+15 Hz of the operating machine frequency. The design shall avoid resonance with the 3rd, 5th and 7th 
harmonic during machine run-up and run-down. 
 
The foundation shall have adequate stiffness and rigidity to prevent movement. 
 
Foundations shall be designed to limit settlements and differential settlements resulting from soil 
consolidation, soil type, permeability etc. and shall be kept within acceptable tolerances in accordance 
with the Synchronous Condenser OEM prescribed operational limits.

The foundation shall be provided with adequate stability by ensuring that the resultant of all forces 
acting on the machine foundation passes through or close to the centre of gravity of the foundation base 
area. 
 
Any cooling, steam or hot air pipes embedded in the foundation shall be properly isolated. 
 
The foundation centre of gravity shall closely align with the centre of gravity of the machine vertically. 
 
The foundation shall be designed to safely withstand static and dynamic loads without experiencing 
bearing capacity and shear failures and cracking. 
 
Where possible, the foundation should be designed in such a manner as to permit a subsequent 
alteration of natural frequency by changing base area or mass of the foundation as may subsequently 
be required.

2.22 Fire wall 
A fire wall shall be provided adjacent to the transformer and facing the Synchronous Condenser installation 
equipment and shall comply with Specification SDC-001 Substation Civil and Structural Design. The wall width 
and height dimensions shall be appropriately designed to provide functional protection to the station and pony 
motor transformers, insulated bus ducting, radiator cooler banks and the main Synchronous Condenser 
building.  
2.23 Noise Enclosures 
The evaluation of noise for motors, transformers, plant etc. and resulting noise enclosures and noise 
suppression controls shall fully comply with Specifications SDC-001 Substation Civil and Structural Design, 
SDE-001 Substation Electrical Design and SSC-423 Transformer Noise Enclosures.

2.24 Site Water Supply 
The site shall be provided with a 9 kilolitre round rainwater polyethylene tank and shall be provided with a 20-
year warranty. 
The rainwater tank shall be positioned such that it can be supplied from the whole Synchronous Condenser 
building gutters. 
The water tank shall be reticulated to the building toilet, sink and shower by means of a suitable pump. The 
pump shall be in a secure, concealed position such that any discharge of water from failure of the pump shall be 
adequately drained. 
The rainwater tank shall be provided with a vermin proof steel stainless steel mesh and sunlight covered 
opening and a 90mm overflow outlet. The overflow outlet shall connect to a 90mm vertical pipe to discharge 
over a gully grate to the stormwater drainage system.

1. Purpose and Scope 
1.1 
Purpose 
a) This document is the Powerlink Queensland Technical Specification for the design of high voltage 
substation civil and structural infrastructure. 
b) The term “Principal” and “Powerlink Queensland” used in this document are interchangeable 
1.2 
Scope 
a) This document provides the technical specification for the necessary components for the design of 
environmental, civil, structural and security infrastructure of high voltage (HV) substations to meet the 
current Powerlink Policies, Standards and Guidelines, Australian and/or International Standards, Codes 
and Guidelines and Government Regulations and Guidelines. 
b) This document covers new and existing installations.

text:
olicies, Standards and Guidelines, Australian and/or International Standards, Codes 
and Guidelines and Government Regulations and Guidelines. 
b) This document covers new and existing installations. Some new and existing installations may need 
non-standard solutions that vary from those specified in this document and will need to be designed to 
suit the alternate circumstances while still meeting the various Standards, Codes, Regulations and 
Guidelines, unless an exemption is obtained. Non-standard solutions will not be accepted by Powerlink 
without prior written approval from the Principal. 
c) Design work referenced by this document generally relates to civil and structural infrastructure within 
the substation fence line but may extend up to and outside the property boundary depending on the 
nature of the installation. Some examples include sediment control, retaining walls, road entry points, 
AC supplies and telecommunications equipment.

2. Introduction 
a) This specification defines requirements for civil and structural design of the primary infrastructure for HV 
electrical substations from 110kV to 500kV.  
b) Primary infrastructure civil and structural design consists of, but is not limited to: 
i. 
Obtaining the necessary site information such as flood levels, geotechnical conditions, soil 
properties and surveying for the design of the site works, environmental controls, platform, 
roads and drainage.

transformer / reactor / capacitor bank foundations and enclosures, noise and fire walls, 
structures, cable duct system, oil containment, fencing, and any other civil or structural

c) This specification shall be read in conjunction with SDE-001 Substation Electrical Design. 
d) Substation demountable buildings are procured under SMM-110 Supply of Substation and

General

substation fence.

on surface water flow and the location of flow inhibiting barriers, e.g. cable trenches etc. 
c) All site drainage and outlets shall be separate from the oil containment drainage. 
d) Any stormwater drain large enough to enable human passage from outside the substation shall have a 
suitable grate at the outlet and shall be locked at both ends.

3.7.4 
Scour and Erosion 
a) Water flows over concrete edges (e.g., edge of headwall base) shall have suitable measures to prevent 
scour and undermining at the concrete edge. Placement of riprap in front of headwalls shall be such 
that it dissipates the water energy and does not cause erosion and undercutting around the headwall 
and riprap. 
b) Due to high likelihood of soil erosion from concentrated water flows through fence kerb slots, discharge 
of water through slots in the fence kerb is not permitted.  
3.7.5 
Outlets 
a) Pipe outlets shall be set into a suitable headwall with energy dissipaters where necessary and suitable 
rock riprap erosion control extending downstream from the headwall apron.

3.7.5 
Outlets 
a) Pipe outlets shall be set into a suitable headwall with energy dissipaters where necessary and suitable 
rock riprap erosion control extending downstream from the headwall apron. 
b) All outlets (and inlets where applicable) for pipes 300mm diameter and greater that come from within or 
pass under a substation and are accessible to the public shall have a suitable grate fitted to prevent a 
person’s access into or under the substation via the drainage system. The grate shall be designed to 
have a tamper proof locking mechanism, that cannot easily be removed for security reasons, and 
minimise the entrapment of rubbish flowing out of the drain. 
c) Signs shall be erected on the inside of the substation fence indicating the locality of drainage pipe 
outlets. The signs shall be 200mm x 150mm, metal, double sided, white with black text stating 
‘Stormwater Outlet’ or ‘Oil Separation Tank Outlet’ as applicable.

3.8 
Equipment and Building Foundations 
3.8.1 
General 
a) Plant, equipment and building foundations shall be designed to suit the site soil conditions based on the 
design loading combinations specified above.  
b) Plant and equipment foundations shall be designed in accordance with Specification GDC-102 
Substation and Transmission Line Structures Foundation Design. 
c) Foundations shall be constructed from reinforced concrete and shall be designed for buoyant conditions 
with the water level at Ground Level. 
d) Foundation drawings shall show the design parameters used for the design of the foundations. 
e) Structures, other than concrete poles shall be designed for baseplate and holding down bolt connection 
to the foundation.

3.8.2 
Structures with Specific Access Requirements 
a) Particular circuit breakers and equipment have the operating cubicles set at a height where normal 
access to the operating points from ground level is difficult without a step. In these cases, a concrete 
platform, minimum size one metre square, shall be constructed where the operator stands.  
b) The platforms elevation shall be at least flush with the top of the underside of the base of the plant or its 
structure or higher where section and ground clearances to the appropriate parts of the circuit breaker 
and surrounding plant permit.

3.8.3 
Holding Down Bolts for General Structures 
a) Holding down bolts shall be a minimum diameter of 16mm for minor, lightly-loaded applications not 
supporting substation plant and a minimum diameter of 24mm for all other applications and shall be 
designed in a square or circular pattern unless otherwise required for structures nominated in this 
specification being supplied by the plant manufacturer. Except for marshalling kiosks all holding down 
bolts shall have an embedment into concrete of not less than one metre. All holding down bolts shall be 
hot-dip galvanized to AS/NZS 4680 over the full length of the bolt.

3.8.4 
Conduits and Earthing Tails 
a) Conduits required in foundations shall be adequately secured to the foundations and shall be protected 
from damage by building-into concrete surrounds or by an accepted alternative. Conduits shall extend a 
minimum of 50mm above the top of the foundations. 
b) Earthing tail rebates, 50mm wide x 30mm deep, shall be provided on all four sides of the foundation cap 
except for gantry towers where only two opposite sides are required. Rebates shall be a minimum of 
150mm below ground level and they shall be aligned with the structure earthing points.

3.8.5 
Circulating Currents in Reinforcing 
a) Where plant with high electromagnetic fields (such as air cored reactors) is capable of inducing 
circulating currents into closed metallic loops, the reinforcing in the foundations and aprons shall be of a 
suitable material type, or isolated, so that closed metallic loops are not formed.

buildings and landings and sloped towards the edges to drain.

3.8.7 
Oil Filled Shunt Reactor and Transformer Foundations 
3.8.7.1 
General 
a) The foundations, drained bunded enclosures, noise walls and fire walls for transformers and oil filled 
reactors shall comply with the requirements of SDE-001 Sections 4.6.2 Reactors and 4.6.3 Power 
Transformers and this specification Sections 3.9 Noise and Fire Walls, 3.15 Oil Containment and 3.16 
Oil Drainage System.  
b) Unless specified otherwise, all new reactor and transformer foundations shall provide for a noise wall 
even if the noise wall is not being installed with the plant. The design drawings for a noise wall shall be 
provided to the Principal and the material choice shall be fully supported by an acoustic noise model in 
compliance with Specification SDE-001.

provided to the Principal and the material choice shall be fully supported by an acoustic noise model in 
compliance with Specification SDE-001.  
c) The bunded enclosure shall be designed as a water/oil tight structure to prevent any oil leakage through 
the concrete, blockwork, jointing or cable conduits in the event of a spill. 
d) Transformer / Reactor foundation aprons and plinths shall have a minimum reinforced thickness of 
450mm and 600mm respectively. 
e) The area between internal road kerbing and bund walls for transformers and reactors shall be prepared, 
graded, compacted and drained to a similar requirement as for internal roads and finished off with an 
earthed 150mm thick S32 reinforced concrete slab where its finished level shall match the gravel layer 
surface, thereby providing a minimum 300kPa load bearing capacity for plant delivery and removal.

3.8.7.2 
Plant Installation Requirements 
a) The bunded enclosure shall be designed to allow the installation of the transformer by crane/s and 
sliding via temporary rails from the road onto the slab and jacking to raise and lower the tank. 
b) The slabs and bund apron shall be designed for the loads from crane stabilising outriggers being placed 
inside the bund to reduce the required crane reach, support dunnage for the slip rails and, from 
hydraulic jacks placed at the jacking points of the main transformer tank. The foundation design shall 
consider any eccentricities caused by the various permanent and short-term loads.

3.8.8 
Low Level Electrical Plant Enclosure Apron 
a) Any area where outdoor low level electrical plant (e.g., Capacitor Bank or air cored reactors) is 
enclosed, the area shall have a concrete apron extending a minimum of 100mm beyond the safety 
fence (i.e., fence mounted on the concrete) such that the growth of vegetation is prevented throughout 
the life of the installation.  
b) A 3-metre-wide x 3-metre-long concrete ramp shall be provided at the gates to the enclosure for access 
into the enclosure by scissor lift or similar small vehicles.

b) A 3-metre-wide x 3-metre-long concrete ramp shall be provided at the gates to the enclosure for access

c) The enclosure apron and plant foundations shall have minimal joints in the concrete and between each 
other. Any joints shall be positioned so that any weeds that may grow in the joints do not cause the low-
level plant to electrically flash over. All joints shall be filled with suitable long-life filler. 
d) Cracking of the concrete base shall be controlled so crack width is minimised preventing weed growth in 
the cracks. 
3.9 
Noise and Fire Walls 
3.9.1 
General 
a) Noise walls and fire walls shall be constructed of robust materials that have a proven minimum 40-year 
service life with no maintenance. The noise wall shall be positioned to avoid pipe supports, valves, 
bellows, flanges and bends being embedded in the wall.

erials that have a proven minimum 40-year

bellows, flanges and bends being embedded in the wall. 
b) Noise walls and fire walls shall comply with specification SDE-001 Substation Electrical Design.  
3.9.2 
Fire Walls 
a) Fire wall barriers shall have a fire resistance level (FRL) of 240/240/240 (structural adequacy, integrity 
and insulation) in accordance with specification SDE-001 Substation Electrical Design for a heat flux of 
150kW per square metre at the bund wall. Barriers shall be as close as possible to the appropriate 
transformer and/or reactor and extend at least 1.8m on both short sides (or to the corner of the bund on 
either side, whichever is the greater) and 0.6m above the oil containing parts, including conservators

a) As transformers and oil filled reactors emit low frequency tonal noise (with the greatest amplitudes 
being at 100, 200 and to a lesser extent 300 Hz), particular emphasis shall be directed to attenuating 
these frequencies in the design of transformer main tank sound enclosures. 
b) The noise enclosure design shall consider both insertion loss and absorption as the most likely 
mechanisms to achieve the required sound level attenuation.

Purpose 
The purpose of this document is to specify the minimum Powerlink requirements and acceptance criteria for the 
provision of construction works for conduits, cable trenches and associated works. 
1.2

works undertaken for Powerlink as specified by the Infrastructure Delivery and Technical Services division in the 
contract documentation.

Substation Construction Works – General other relevant Powerlink’s technical specifications, and approved for 
construction drawings.

a) Conduits shall be installed along the routes shown on construction drawings. Any rerouting of conduits 
shall be subject to review and acceptance by Powerlink prior to installation. 
b) The Contractor shall install conduits true to line and grade commencing at the lower ends of all lines and 
working in an upward direction to the following tolerances:  
• 
trench and excavation centrelines shall be correctly positioned ±50 mm; 
• 
conduits and cable pits shall be aligned in plan as specified ±6 mm, except that the maximum 
deviation from straightness in any 3-metre length shall be 6 mm; 
• 
all inverts shall be to the specified levels ±5 mm, and shall be free draining; and 
• 
all joints shall be internally flush ±2 mm, smooth and watertight. 
c) Multiple conduit runs shall be installed with at least 50 mm minimum clear separation between conduits, 
unless shown otherwise in construction drawings.

e) The ends of buried conduits shall be marked with white painted timber stakes.  
f) 
One (1) 8 mm diameter synthetic draw rope shall be supplied and installed in each electrical conduit 
run. 
g) Bell mouths shall be supplied and installed where cable conduits enter cable pits and trenches. Where 
the use of bell mouths is not practical, the concrete edges shall be rounded off to a minimum radius of 
20 mm. 
h) Reinforced concrete slabs shall be constructed to cover conduits where shown on construction

Backfilling Cable Pits, Cable Trenches and Conduits 
2.9.1 Concrete Curing and Formwork Removal 
a) The formwork shall not be removed around concrete pits until the concrete has gained sufficient strength to 
avoid structural damage to the pit or damage to the concrete surfaces. This period shall not be less than 48 
hours after placing the concrete. 
b) Backfilling around concrete pits or cable trenches shall not commence until the concrete has gained 
sufficient strength to avoid structural damage or damage to the concrete surfaces, with a minimum period of 
72 hours after placing the concrete.

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
a) The purpose of this document is to define the technical requirements for the fabrication, delivery and 
storage of substation steel structures 
1.2 
Scope 
a) This document covers the supply of materials, including fasteners and accessories, fabrication, trial 
assembly of lattice strain beams and tower structures, galvanizing, sub-assembly as required, delivery 
to site and storage on site of all steelwork. 
2. Steelwork Materials 
a) All structural steel, fasteners and welding electrodes shall comply with Section 2 of AS 4100 together 
with the requirements of this Specification.

a) All structural steel, fasteners and welding electrodes shall comply with Section 2 of AS 4100 together

b) For structural steel manufactured overseas, the material used in the manufacture shall comply with AS 
4100 Section 2 Materials and shall be certified by a JAS-ANZ accredited independent specialist auditing

AS/NZS ISO/IEC 17000. 
c) Unidentified steel shall not be used.

capacity of the member, its ability to be adequately welded, or the quality of the galvanized surface.

4. Galvanizing 
4.1 
General 
a) All ferrous items shall be hot dip galvanized in accordance with AS/NZS 4680 after all fabrication is 
completed. Bolts and nuts shall be effectively hot dip galvanized in accordance with AS/NZS 1214.  
b) The zinc coating shall be adherent, smooth, continuous and thorough, free from lumps, drips, blisters, 
gritty areas, uncoated spots, acid and black spots, dross and flux or other defects.  
c) Irrespective of any referenced standards, the mass of zinc coating per square metre of surface area of 
ferrous items shall not be less than 600 grams.  
d) Particular care shall be taken in the handling and storage of galvanized steelwork to minimise damage 
and avoid the occurrence of "white rust".

text:
ferrous items shall not be less than 600 grams.  
d) Particular care shall be taken in the handling and storage of galvanized steelwork to minimise damage 
and avoid the occurrence of "white rust". Reference should be made to the provisions of AS/NZS 4680.  
e) Care must be exercised during “pickling” of the steel by limiting the exposure time of steel in the acid 
bath to prevent the onset of hydrogen embrittlement.  
f) 
All galvanized steelwork shall be passivated in a 0.1% sodium dichromate solution.  
g) After hot-dip galvanizing, the maximum allowable bow, in any of the main members shall not exceed 1 
in 500 measured along any plane.  
4.2 
Repair of Damaged Galvanizing 
Any galvanising damage or defects shall be repaired as follows: 
a) For individual areas less than 1000 mm2 that are not at a welded connection or where the sum of the 
individual areas on a single member are less than 0.2%; the rust free member may be repaired on site.

text:
individual areas less than 1000 mm2 that are not at a welded connection or where the sum of the 
individual areas on a single member are less than 0.2%; the rust free member may be repaired on site. 
The members shall be repaired by the application of at least two coats of a zinc metal paint system 
containing 95% metallic zinc in the dried film. The paint shall be based on an accepted organic single 
component coating with self-rejuvenating qualities for recoating, repairing or replenishing. The paint 
system shall be suitable for brush applications in relative humidity up to 95% with substrate 
temperatures between -15 and +40 degrees Celsius and shall have a current APAS 2916/2 certification. 
The treated surfaces shall be prepared in accordance with the paint manufacturer’s requirements.

Hot Zinc Metal Spray Repair 
a) Preparation of the steel surfaces shall be to Class Sa3, in accordance with AS 1627.4. Cleaned 
surfaces shall be handled with clean gloves only, prior to metallising.

text:
Hot Zinc Metal Spray Repair 
a) Preparation of the steel surfaces shall be to Class Sa3, in accordance with AS 1627.4. Cleaned 
surfaces shall be handled with clean gloves only, prior to metallising. The prepared surface shall be 
metallised with hot metallic zinc spray in accordance with ISO 2063-2 the sprayed coating being applied 
as soon as possible after surface preparation and within four hours of completion of the blast 
preparation. The zinc wire shall be in accordance with BS EN 1179 for Zn3. The zinc metal shall be 
applied at the rate of 1800 gm/m2 of metallised area and the final deposited thickness, checked with an 
accepted thickness meter, shall be not less than 175 microns.

a) During temporary storage on site, sufficient dunnage or seasoned timber packing shall be supplied as 
temporary supports for the steelwork to maintain a minimum clearance of 100mm above ground level. 
b) All steelwork and structures shall be placed such that no undue stress is placed on members, plates, 
bolts or threads. No structure shall be placed on top of another.

occurrence of "white rust". The handling and storage shall comply with the provisions and 
recommendations of Appendix F of AS/NZS 4680.

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
a) The purpose of this document is to define deliverables related to the fabrication, delivery and storage of 
substation steel structures described in the Technical Requirements SMC-109.1. 
1.2 
Scope 
b) The scope of this document defines the deliverables and control points in relation to the supply of 
materials, including fasteners and accessories, fabrication, trial assembly of lattice strain beam and 
tower structures, galvanizing, sub-assembly as required, delivery to site and storage on site of all 
steelwork described in the Technical Requirements SMC-109.1. 
2. General 
a) The Contractor shall perform all the works and supply all the materials specified in SMC-109.1.

2. General 
a) The Contractor shall perform all the works and supply all the materials specified in SMC-109.1. 
b) The Contractor will not be required to prepare designs or drawings, except for workshop detail drawings 
for all steelwork and structures if required for manufacturing purposes. 
3. Steelwork Materials 
a) Where the Principal accepts use of steel grades that differ from grades defined on drawings, such steel 
shall be clearly identified at all stages of fabrication. 
b) The Specification requires that all materials comply with one or more Australian Standards. Where 
current certificates cannot be provided, the Principal may direct the Contractor to carry out any tests set 
out in any such Standard. All costs of testing of materials shall be borne by the Contractor. All test 
certificates shall carry a National Association of Testing Authorities (NATA) endorsement.

4. Fabrication 
a) All the required testing and eventual consequential repairs cost and time shall be borne by the 
Contractor. 
b) The Contractor shall submit copies of all ultrasonic test results to the Principal prior to dispatch of the 
relevant items to the galvanizer (Hold Point). 
c) Any certificates of inspections or tests will not relieve the Contractor’s liability for faulty workmanship or 
faulty materials which may become evident before expiry of the defects liability period. 
d) The Contractor shall give the Principal at least five (5) working days' notice of when fabricated items are 
to be sent for galvanizing so that pre-galvanizing inspections and acceptance may be carried out 
(Witness Point).

repairs (Witness Point).

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
The purpose of this specification is to define the minimum requirements for design, fabrication and delivery of 
Substation and Communications demountable buildings. 
1.2 
Scope 
The scope of this document covers the detailed specification for design, fabrication and delivery to nominated 
locations of substation and communications buildings. 
2. Substation and Communications Buildings 
Substation and communications buildings covered by this specification comprise the following types: 
(i) 
Prefabricated buildings that are fabricated and assembled in a factory workshop, then delivered to a 
specified location.

(i) 
Prefabricated buildings that are fabricated and assembled in a factory workshop, then delivered to a

3. Prefabricated Buildings Common Requirements 
3.1 
General 
a) The Contractor shall design, supply drawings and documentation, manufacture, test and deliver 
prefabricated, transportable buildings, including building supports, to a nominated location for: 
(i) Control building to house fixed frame and swing frame electrical control panels and battery 
banks with typical layouts shown on drawings H-131843-110 to 113 (11 m building) and H-
131843-114 to 117 (14 m building). Non typical layouts may be required for individual projects. 
(ii) Communications building to house communications equipment and battery banks with typical 
layouts shown on drawings H-131843-140 to H-131843-143.

(ii) Communications building to house communications equipment and battery banks with typical

(iii) Amenities building to house a lunchroom, office desk and washroom facilities with typical 
layouts shown on drawings H-131843-130 to 132. Non typical layouts may be required for 
individual projects. 
(iv) Combined control, communications and amenities buildings with typical layouts shown on 
drawings H-131843-120 to H-131843-123 where specified for small substations. Non typical

3.2 
Design criteria 
a) The design shall ensure the structural integrity of the building during construction, transportation, 
storage (if required), installation and design service life. 
b) The building shall be suitable for the housing of electronic equipment.  
c) The building shall be constructed such that it is sealed to prevent dust and vermin entering the building 
or external cabinets. 
d) Spaces and voids above the cable termination cubicles shall be closed off by fitment of flashing to 
prevent the entering/nesting of vermin and birds.

a) The general cable ladder and PVC cable duct requirements are summarised below. Example photos of

Substation sites

Additional requirements for communications sites

repeater site with backup diesel generator), the AC switchboard shall be a special design with an

a) The building shall be supplied and fitted with internal cable trays as outlined on the specification

Wind loads 
a) Design shall be in accordance with Australian Steel Institute’s, Wind Actions on Steel Sheds and

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
The purpose of this document is to specify the minimum Powerlink requirements and acceptance criteria for the 
provision of construction works for erection of steel structures. 
1.2 
Scope 
This specification applies to all steel structure erection works and associated construction activities undertaken 
for Powerlink. These works are to be carried out as detailed in the contract documentation provided by the 
Infrastructure Delivery and Technical Services division  
This specification shall be read in conjunction with Australian Standards, Powerlink’s Specification SSG-426 
Substation Construction Works - General, other relevant Powerlink’s technical specifications, and approved for 
construction drawings.

2. Erection of Steel Structures 
2.1 
General 
a) This section covers the construction requirements for erection of steel structures in substations and 
telecommunication sites.  
b) All clauses within this section are written in the imperative shall be carried out by the Contractor, unless 
otherwise stated. 
c) The Contractor shall comply with all relevant legislative and technical requirements for the erection of 
steel structures.  
d) The steel structures shall be assembled and erected in accordance with the construction drawings, this 
specification and equipment manufacturer’s requirements where applicable. 
e) Holding down bolts, nuts and washers shall be supplied as a part of the foundation as specified in 
Powerlink’s Specification SSC-421 Foundations.

text:
nt manufacturer’s requirements where applicable. 
e) Holding down bolts, nuts and washers shall be supplied as a part of the foundation as specified in 
Powerlink’s Specification SSC-421 Foundations.  
f) 
Drilling or modification of steel structures is not permitted unless otherwise accepted in writing by 
Powerlink. 
2.2 
Storage of Steelwork 
a) The Contractor shall ensure that steelwork does not suffer damage or deterioration during handling, 
transport and storage.  
b) During storage on site, the Contractor shall supply sufficient dunnage or seasoned timber packing as 
temporary supports for the steelwork to maintain a minimum clearance of 100 mm above ground level. 
c) All steel structures shall be placed on temporary supports such that no undue stress is placed on 
members, plates, bolts or threads.  
d) Where temporary transportation packaging may create contamination of surface coating, such 
packaging shall be removed and disposed accordingly.

e) The Contractor shall take particular care in the handling and storage of galvanised steelwork to avoid 
the occurrence of ’white rust’ and shall comply with the provisions and recommendations in AS 4680 
Appendix F. 
2.3 
Erection of Steel Structures 
a) Where steel structures are provided by Powerlink or by the equipment supplier (e.g. circuit breakers and 
isolators), the steel structures shall be: 
• 
delivered to site with the respective equipment; and  
• 
fully assembled by the Contractor into the sections shown on the construction drawings and erected 
on foundations.  
b) All other steel structures supplied by the Contractor shall be fully assembled into sections shown on the 
construction drawings and erected on foundations.

2.5 
Repair of Damaged Galvanising 
a) Special care shall be taken not to damage the galvanised coating of the steel structure during erection. 
b) Where repair of damaged galvanising is being considered, the Contractor shall submit (SUBMISSION) 
the proposed repair methods for review and acceptance (HOLD POINT) by Powerlink prior to the repair 
being undertaken. The repair method shall be supported by relevant information including 
manufacturers’ requirements. Any repairs shall not diminish the strength or impede the operation of the 
steel structure. 
c) Minor damage as defined in AS 1650 may be repaired at site, by the application of at least two coats of 
a zinc rich paint (accepted by Powerlink) to rust free steel. 
d) Areas of larger damage, but not exceeding 4000 mm2 may be repaired by the application of zinc metal 
spray or low melting point zinc alloy repair rods (accepted by Powerlink) or by regalvanising.

spray or low melting point zinc alloy repair rods (accepted by Powerlink) or by regalvanising. 
e) Damaged areas in excess of 4000 mm2 shall be regalvanised. 
f) 
In areas of coastal exposure, Powerlink may require all damaged items to be regalvanised. 
2.6 
Earthing of Steel Structures 
The temporary and final earthing of steel structures shall be done in accordance with Powerlink’s Specification 
SSE-427 Electrical Works. 
2.7

1. Introduction 
1.1 
Purpose 
The purpose of this document is to specify the minimum Powerlink requirements and acceptance criteria for the 
provision of construction works for electrical plant and equipment. 
1.2 
Scope 
This specification applies to all electrical works and associated construction and installation works undertaken 
for Powerlink as specified by the Infrastructure Delivery and Technical Services division in the contract 
documentation. 
This specification shall be read in conjunction with Australian Standards, Powerlink’s Specification SSG-426 
Substation Construction Works - General, other relevant Powerlink’s technical specifications, and approved for 
construction drawings.

on with Australian Standards, Powerlink’s Specification SSG-426 
Substation Construction Works - General, other relevant Powerlink’s technical specifications, and approved for

Where conflict exists between this specification and the Australian Standards, Powerlink’s Specification SSG-
426 Substation Construction Works - General or other relevant Powerlink’s technical specifications, this 
specification shall take precedence.  
Where conflict exists between this specification and construction drawings, the construction drawings shall take 
precedence. 
2. Electrical Works in Substation 
2.1 
General 
a) This specification covers the construction requirements for electrical plant and equipment construction 
and installation works in substations and telecommunication sites.  
b) All clauses within this document is written in the imperative shall be carried out by the Contractor, 
unless otherwise stated.
source: 10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf

text:
and installation works in substations and telecommunication sites.  
b) All clauses within this document is written in the imperative shall be carried out by the Contractor, 
unless otherwise stated. 
c) The Contractor shall comply with all relevant legislative including the Electricity Act and may need to 
comply with AS/NZS 3000 for LV AC installations (e.g. low level lighting, GPOs, electrical installation in 
buildings, etc.). 
d) In operational substations, electrical plant and equipment construction and installation works shall be 
planned and executed while maintaining access into and around the substation. 
e) All electrical equipment connections, including secondary systems connections, shall be completed or 
terminated by a currently licensed Electrical Worker who holds a current Open Electrical Work Licence 
from WorkCover Queensland and is familiar with substation works.

f) 
At Practical Completion, the Contractor shall submit (SUBMISSION) to Powerlink the following for each 
item of plant and equipment installed and tested: 
• 
a vendor release for circuit breakers (refer to section 3.4), capacitor banks (refer to section 3.9; and 
DC system (refer to section 3.11); 
• 
all completed Inspection Test Plans (ITPs); and 
• 
Inspection Test Records (ITRs). 
g) The minimum time limits for erecting strung and rigid bus following concreting of footings shall be: 
• 
Conductor stringing between plant with spans <= 10m – 21 days 
• 
Conductor stringing with spans > 10m – 28 days 
• 
Erection of rigid (tubular) bus bars – 21 days

2.2 
Electrical and Safety Clearances 
a) Unless otherwise specified by Powerlink, the Contractor shall comply with the legislative electrical and 
safety clearance for exclusion zone.  
b) Any works likely to encroach within 6 m of in service plant shall require the Contractor to follow 
Powerlink’s Notice of Intention to Perform Task (NIPT) process as specified in Powerlink’s Work Health 
and Safety (WHS) Specification. 
2.3 
Strung Bus 
a) The strung bus refers to all overhead conductors include the associated insulator assemblies and 
hardware.  
b) The strung bus shall be erected as shown in construction drawings. 
c) All strung bus spanning the HV plant shall be in place prior to the erection of the HV plant.
source: 10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf
source_path: /mnt/c/Users/z0051yym/Desktop/test_bp_code/knowledge_graph_vector_GC_Data/graph-rag-se-datamodel/data/pdfs/syncon/GC25_122_SynCon_4x_Powerlink/1_Contract_documents/0_RFP/10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf

text:
tor assemblies and 
hardware.  
b) The strung bus shall be erected as shown in construction drawings. 
c) All strung bus spanning the HV plant shall be in place prior to the erection of the HV plant. Where this is 
not possible, suitable mechanical protection shall be placed to protect HV plant. The mechanical 
protection shall be inspected (HOLD POINT) by Powerlink prior to commencing with installation of the 
strung bus. 
d) The strung bus conductor shall be supplied to Site on wooden or steel drums. Drums shall be stored on 
level ground with the axis horizontal and shall not be dropped from vehicles or distorted in any way 
which causes difficulty in running off the conductor. The protecting battens must remain in place on the 
drums as long as possible to prevent damage to the outer layers of conductor. 
e) The conductor shall be supported above ground on cable rollers or similar once it has been run off the 
drum and prior to being erected.
source: 10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf
source_path: /mnt/c/Users/z0051yym/Desktop/test_bp_code/knowledge_graph_vector_GC_Data/graph-rag-se-datamodel/data/pdfs/syncon/GC25_122_SynCon_4x_Powerlink/1_Contract_documents/0_RFP/10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf

text:
ssible to prevent damage to the outer layers of conductor. 
e) The conductor shall be supported above ground on cable rollers or similar once it has been run off the 
drum and prior to being erected. Vehicles must be prohibited from driving over the conductor, and 
pedestrians must be prohibited from walking on the conductor. 
f) 
Every precaution shall be taken to ensure that conductors, when erected, are left without any scratches, 
cuts, protruding stands, bird caging, rough welds, deposits of grease or dirt, deformation or adhesions. 
g) Only conductor, which is free of imperfections, shall be used for a compression termination. All grease 
and foreign matter shall be wiped away and any light scratches shall be removed by rubbing down with 
fine emery cloth. The insulator assembly shall be inspected (WITNESS POINT) by Powerlink prior to 
the installation of the insulator assembly on the gantry or support structure.
source: 10 Section 3a - Exhibit 3 Specification - SMM-193 Supply of Synchronous Condenser and other Technical Specifications.pdf

text:
by rubbing down with 
fine emery cloth. The insulator assembly shall be inspected (WITNESS POINT) by Powerlink prior to 
the installation of the insulator assembly on the gantry or support structure.  
h) The erection of the connections between the strung bus and droppers shall be carried out from a 
certified elevated work platform. The certified elevated work platform shall be earthed when working 
within an operational substation. Construction earths to be placed where applicable. 
i)

4.4.5 
Extension of Earthing Grid and Connections to Fencing 
a) When extending the earthing grid within or adjacent to an operational substation, the Contractor shall 
give due consideration to the risks associated with transferred potential in the event of an earth fault 
occurring during installation of the conductors. 
b) The Contractor shall submit (SUBMISSION) a Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS) for Powerlink’s 
review and acceptance (HOLD POINT). The SWMS shall indicate how related hazards shall be 
managed and shall include Powerlink’s requirements as set out below. 
• 
Prior to commencing the installation of the conductors the Contractor shall establish a 3 metre 
isolation zone; 
• 
The Contractor shall always work towards the existing grid.

as set out below. 
• 
Prior to commencing the installation of the conductors the Contractor shall establish a 3 metre 
isolation zone; 
• 
The Contractor shall always work towards the existing grid. The installation shall commence at the 
perimeter of the Site and progress in stages towards the existing grid; and 
• 
The work covered in each stage shall be fully completed prior to the next stage commencing i.e., all 
conductors must be installed, all connections must be made, inspected (HOLD POINT) by 
Powerlink and all excavations are to be backfilled and compacted. 
4.4.5.1 Stage 1: Installation of Earthing and Fencing Outside the Isolation Zone 
a) The first stage of the work shall incorporate the installation of all earthing and fencing up to the outside 
of the isolation zone.

text:
nstallation of Earthing and Fencing Outside the Isolation Zone 
a) The first stage of the work shall incorporate the installation of all earthing and fencing up to the outside 
of the isolation zone. 
b) The Contractor shall ensure that no conductive material breaches the isolation zone until this stage is 
completed, including but not limited to: 
• 
earthing conductor; 
• 
fencing material; and 
• 
AC supply cabling for construction use (unless electrical isolation is provided). 
c) Safety requirements such as gloves and insulating mats are not required during this stage as long as 
the isolation zone is not breached. 
4.4.5.2 Stage 2: Installation of Earthing and Fencing Across the Isolation Zone 
a) The second stage of the work involves connecting the conductors and fencing across the isolation zone 
to the existing grid. The work is of higher risk and shall be completed as quickly as possible.

text:
The second stage of the work involves connecting the conductors and fencing across the isolation zone 
to the existing grid. The work is of higher risk and shall be completed as quickly as possible.  
b) The principle of always working towards the existing grid shall be adhered to as much as possible. 
c) During this stage, insulating gloves shall be used whenever conductors are handled.  
d) When connections are made to the existing grid, the following minimum safety requirements shall be 
implemented: 
• 
insulating mats as well as gloves shall be used; 
• 
temporary jumper leads are to be applied between the existing grid and the new conductor. The 
jumper shall match the existing earth grid; 
• 
the new fence shall not be extended across the isolation zone until the earthing is completely 
finished; and 
• 
the modified extended earth grid shall be considered to be non-compliant with AS 2067 and

The purpose of this document is to specify the minimum Powerlink requirements and acceptance criteria for the 
provision of electrical testing associated with construction works of electrical plant and equipment in substations.

This specification applies to all electrical construction testing undertaken on Powerlink substation assets as 
specified by the Infrastructure Delivery and Technical Services Division.

Construction Testing – refers to the electrical testing and inspection that prove construction works conform to 
approved construction drawings (namely, electrical erection and electrical installations). Among others, 
construction testing includes testing the functionality of primary equipment, by the Contractor or by others, point-
to-point cable verification, visual inspections, continuity testing, and insulation resistance measurements. 
Construction testing does not include proving the system integration between secondary system equipment and 
field equipment. 
Primary Plant/Equipment refers to all equipment which directly transports High Voltage (HV) electricity.

Primary Plant/Equipment refers to all equipment which directly transports High Voltage (HV) electricity. Some 
examples of Primary equipment are switchgear, instrumentation transformers, power transformers, HV 
conductors (Busbar, strung conductor and HV Cable), etc. 
Secondary System(s) refers to the Substation Automation System (SAS), the substation protection systems, 
data networks, telecommunications networks and all other equipment, conductors and cables which do not 
directly transport HV electricity. The circuitry included in primary plant and the Low Voltage (LV) windings/taps 
of Instrument Transformers are also considered secondary systems. 
Site Infrastructure is a subset of the secondary systems that specifically refers to equipment that supports the 
secondary systems for protection, control and operation of primary plant.

secondary systems for protection, control and operation of primary plant. Examples of site infrastructure are 
Alternating Current (AC) supply, changeover and distribution systems; Direct Current (DC) supply and 
distribution systems, and fire and security systems. 
Intelligent Electronic Device (IED) is a generic term used to describe microprocessor-based equipment used to 
protect, monitor and/or control power system equipment e.g. Protection Relays, Remote Terminal Units (RTUs), 
Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) etc. 
Earthing (and Earthing Systems) refers to all Primary and secondary equipment earthing connections, the 
substation combined earthing system and all equipotential bonding conductors and systems.

Primary Plant Installation

drawings.

performed and results recorded for the High Voltage electrical installation: 
 
Verify nameplate details match primary plant installation. i.e.; for a transformer installation check 
primary, secondary, and tertiary connections are as specified for the installation; or the reactor or 
capacitor bank ratings are correct. 
 
Verify and record that serial numbers and operational numbering is correct.

The application of this Standard will ensure that Powerlink Queensland personnel and specific Maintenance 
Service Provider personnel are trained and competent to support Powerlink plant and equipment.
1.1
Purpose

personnel in order to support Powerlink plant and equipment.  
1.2

The requirements of this Standard apply to all primary plant and secondary equipment, including 
telecommunications equipment.
1.3

2. Levels of Training
Six levels of training are required to support the ongoing maintenance and operation of plant and equipment.  
These are:
2.1
Level 1 – System Familiarisation
This level is to support investment and operating decisions. It requires a general knowledge of the equipment and 
may be required by roles which are not directly related to the maintenance and/or fault rectification but rather 
require a general or high level overview of the plant and/or equipment these roles may include Project Sponsors, 
Strategies, NSC operators and emergency response event managers.
2.2
Level 2 – First Callout / Switching Operators

simple component replacement rectifies the fault. Where the secondary systems are integrated, complex, and

irrespective of the equipment location.

should establish at the beginning of the project.

Task 6: Insulation Coordination - Lightning overvoltage study
This study covers the requirements with respect to fast-front lightning overvoltages.
An insulation coordination study will be performed for the main components of the SynCon
connected to the same 345 kV substation. The simulations will be performed using
PSCAD™/EMTDC™.
The lightning surge overvoltage protection study will be performed based on the final layout
of the 345 kV substation and the incoming overhead lines and cable connections (if applicable)
and will include the rating of surge arresters based on maximum continuous operating voltages
and possible temporary overvoltages in case of earth faults.
Overhead lines connected to the substation via cables should be considered, too.

and possible temporary overvoltages in case of earth faults.

Based on the protection characteristic of the surge arresters and on the lightning performance
of the transmission lines, the maximum stresses in the substation and at the SynCon
transformers’ terminals caused by typical lightning strikes (direct strikes to conductors, strikes
to last towers) will be calculated for selected unfavourable substation configurations with one
overhead line linked to the bay of the SynCon only (dead-end configuration). For the analysis,
a base condition of two overhead lines per substation are considered within this scope of work.
It is assumed that the lines that are shared with the SynCon connections (same bay) will be

This study covers the requirements with respect to slow-front switching overvoltages.
An insulation coordination study with focus on switching overvoltages will be performed for

overvoltages originated at the 345 kV level due to:

Switching of network faults

Load rejections

Project Deliverables
The main Project Deliverable is the Final Report for each study comprising a text document and
further annexes as appropriate. It will be provided as soft copy (Adobe *.pdf format). All project
deliverables are in English language.
Single line diagrams with selected calculation results as plotted by the corresponding
calculation software package are also provided in electronic format (Adobe *.pdf and/or
enhanced metafile *.emf). Further relevant data, excluding models, of intermediate and/or
final project results may be provided in suitable format and quantities.
Within 30 calendar days from receipt of formal Project Deliverables, especially the Final
Report, the Client shall check completeness and correctness of the deliverables and approve or
comment.

6 Environmental Responsibility
Environmental protection is a corporate responsibility, social responsibility, and an important
success factor for Siemens Energy. In all units of the company and in all countries in which we
operate, it is our goal to protect the environment and conserve resources.
The Siemens Energy environmental programs are designed to conserve resources throughout
the entire product life-cycle, reduce waste for disposal, and make our own business activities
CO2-neutral. The Siemens Energy Environmental Portfolio is our and our company’s response
to climate change, resource scarcity, and threats to the environment.
Our company meets the ecological demands of its partners by developing future-oriented and
resource efficient solutions, products, and business models.
